title: Read the site language from site.lang
description:
This PR makes `site.lang` the key for the site's language, the name Quarto uses. great-docs read it from a top-level `language:`, while the documentation still taught `site.language`, and Quarto's own `language` key means something else (string overrides).

`site.language` keeps working; a top-level `language:` is no longer read, and `great-docs lint` now warns about both.

title: Remove the unreachable User Guide navigation label
description: This PR removes the post-render code that filled an empty narrow-screen navigation title with a "User Guide" label. Quarto now fills that title itself, with breadcrumbs or the page title, so the label could only appear on a sidebar page that has no title.

title: Use CSS for the end rule on an API Page
description: This PR moves the thin rule at the end of an objects API pages into the theme stylesheet and instead of adding a tag in the post-render.

title: Drop dead reference index rewrites from post-render
description: This PR removes two rewrites of the API reference index page from the post-render step. One converted two-column tables into definition lists and the other removed an "API Reference" entry from the table of contents. Neither can fire on current output: the index already renders its sections as definition lists, and the page title no longer appears as a heading.

title: Label reference pages in the narrow-screen navigation bar without rewriting HTML
description:
This PR movesrewriting Quarto's HTML to label reference pages in the navigation bar shown on narrow screens from the post-render.

Instead of rewriting, a similar visual effect is achieved by styling with css.

title: Write translations and text direction during rendering
description: This PR has non-English pages get their translation bundle, and right-to-left sites their text direction, when Quarto renders them. Until now a post-render step rewrote every finished HTML file: it inserted the gd-i18n meta tag and added dir="rtl" to <html> with a regex. It also emitted a gd-rtl meta tag that nothing reads, which is now gone.

title: feat: add a wide layout toggle for desktop screens
description: This PR implements a wide layout toggle option for desktop screens. When the viewport is 1600 px and up, a new floating button (above the back-to-top buttons) lets readers widen the content column (up to 1.5×) and both sidebars (up to 1.2×). Both sidebars stay visible. Once the layout reaches its maximum, it stays centered rather than stretching across ultrawide displays. The default layout doesn't change: on every page with a sidebar, the default grid is pixel-identical to Quarto's original template. The columns animate to their new widths, and the page keeps the reader's place while text reflows. Readers who prefer reduced motion get an instant switch. The choice is saved in `localStorage` and applied before the first paint, so pages don't flash the narrow layout. The button only appears on pages with a navigation sidebar (User Guide, API reference, custom sections). Below the viewport threshold every page uses the default layout. The `w` keyboard shortcut toggles it and is listed in the help overlay. Labels are translated into all supported languages. Here's the configuration (`wide_layout`, enabled by default): ```yaml wide_layout: enabled: true default: normal # or "wide" content_scale: 1.5 sidebar_scale: 1.2 min_viewport: 1600 prose_max_width: null # e.g. "110ch" to cap prose line length in wide mode ``` The floating-sidebar grid templates in `great-docs.scss` now compute their track sizes from one registered `` property, `--gd-wide-t`, which goes from 0 (default) to 1 (wide). One transition animates the whole grid. Before widening: After widening: Fixes: #362

title: Translate API reference headings and labels during rendering
description: This PR has the API reference write its headings and labels in the site language when it renders the page. Until now a post-render step swapped English text out of the finished HTML. It missed some labels: the Source link was never translated, and translated Note callouts were only caught when Quarto left them in English.

title: Generate social cards during the build instead of after render
description: This PR moves the Open Graph and Twitter card tags out of the post-render script. Post-render added them by reading each page's title and description back out of the rendered HTML, and only when SEO was enabled, though the user guide says the two features are independent. Sites with `seo.enabled: false` therefore had no social cards.

title: Require great_tables 1.1 for the docs extra
description:
This PR removes the cap that held `great_tables` below 0.22 in the docs extra.

Version 0.22 added a dependency on `multimark`, which had no WebAssembly wheel (required by marimo notebooks to be exported and run in the browser under Pyodide). `multimark` 0.4.0 now publishes a WebAssembly wheel.

title: Write page descriptions before rendering
description:
This PR moves the `<meta name="description">` tag out of post-render, where it was taken from the first long-enough paragraph of the rendered HTML. On API pages that paragraph was usually too short, so every reference page showed the site's default description in search results instead of its docstring summary.

Homepages that open with a hero or badges got the default in the same way. Nothing told the author that a page had fallen back to the default, so `great-docs lint --check descriptions` now reports those pages.

title: fix: rewrite a page's metadata only when it changes
description:
This PR stops the pre-render metadata pass from rewriting pages that already carry their head tags.

The pass checked for existing JSON-LD by searching the page source for the tag it had written. With py-yaml12 0.1.0, the version in `uv.lock`, the tag is stored as a double-quoted YAML string with escaped quotes, so the search misses it. Every build then rewrote the homepage and reference pages, and `test_json_ld_written_once` fails locally. CI passed because `pip install -e ".[dev]"` ignores the lock and installs py-yaml12 0.2.0, which stores the tag unescaped in a folded block.

title: refactor: write JSON-LD structured data before rendering
description:
This PR moves the JSON-LD structured data out of the post-render script. Post-render opened every rendered HTML page and spliced the script in before `</head>`, so the data lived in a separate step from the rest of the page metadata, which great-docs already writes before Quarto renders. Pages now get the script through their head tags like the description and social card tags. The values and the pages that carry them are unchanged.

The script is now also escaped, so a package description containing `</script>` can no longer end it early.

title: feat: write page scale-to-fit tags before rendering
description:
This PR moves the per-page scale-to-fit tag out of the post-render script and into each page's front matter before Quarto renders it. Post-render found the tag's selectors by mapping each rendered HTML file back to a `.qmd` source and re-reading its front matter. Pages written in `.md` therefore never got their overrides, and `scale-to-fit` or `scale-to-fit-min-scale` set in a directory `_metadata.yml` was ignored.

Both keys now work in `.md` pages and in `_metadata.yml`, merged the way Quarto merges metadata. Directory selector lists add up from the outermost directory inwards, the nearest directory's minimum scale wins, and a key in the page's own front matter replaces the directory value.

Versioned sites previewed with `great-docs build --watch` also get their page metadata again. Watch mode skips the per-version pipeline, so those pages were missing their scale-to-fit tags, search descriptions and social card options.

title: refactor: mark the Skills page noindex before rendering
description:
This PR moves the robots `noindex` tag for the generated Skills page out of the post-render step and into the page's front matter, so Quarto writes it into the head with the other metadata. Post-render had to scan every rendered page for a `skills.html` path to find the one page that needed the tag.

Matching on the path also caught user pages: a `skills.qmd` in any subdirectory was marked noindex and dropped from search results. Only the generated Skills page carries the tag now. Sites with `seo.enabled: false` still get no robots tag.

title: refactor: share one mechanism for tags in the page head
description:
This PR gives every feature that adds tags to a page's `<head>` one shared path into the page front matter. Before, page dates owned the only list of head tags and wrote it as inline raw HTML, so a second feature writing the same key would have produced a duplicate front matter key and stopped the render. Backticks in values also had to be turned into character references to keep the raw HTML spans intact.

The bundled metadata partial now emits these tags on every build, not only when SEO, translations, social cards or page dates are on. Pages without tags render the same head as before. Page date tags now appear ahead of the translation and Open Graph tags.

title: Add page dates and authors during the build instead of after render
description:
This PR moves the page dates and authors that show_dates adds out of the post-render script. 

Post-render also guessed each rendered page's source file from its path, so it looked for the user guide only in the project root and found no source for sections, blog posts or custom pages. A site with `docs/user_guide`, or with any of those pages, showed no dates on them.

title: fix: modify tooltip placement and fix label updates for floating page buttons
description: Both the back-to-top and wide layout toggle buttons now show their enhanced tooltips to the left (avoiding overlap with each other) and use `data-tippy-content` instead of `title` so the label updates correctly on state changes. The back-to-top button also picks up its i18n translation (translations already present in the codebase) instead of hardcoding English.

title: refactor: type-check the site generators under strict pyright
description:
This PR extends strict pyright from the renderer to the website generator, the API reference generator, the configuration module, and the interlinks, layout migration and pandoc packages. Before, parsed YAML, front matter and site configuration reached most of this code as values of unknown type, so pyright could not check how they were read. Front matter was also split from a page in several places, each with its own rules. `make type-check-strict` now checks every module that passes, and the strict set grows as each module is cleaned up.

Typing the code exposed several crashes and misreadings, which are fixed. Documenting a namespace package crashed while linking its source. A site whose `include-in-header` was a single mapping crashed when adding translated navigation prefixes. An interlinks alias written as a string, such as `aliases: np`, was split into one alias per character. Unusual but valid YAML, such as front matter that is a list, no longer stops the build.

Front matter is now read the way Quarto reads it: it must start on the first line of the page, and a `---` inside a value no longer ends the block. A new `great-docs lint --check front-matter` warns when a page gives a key that great-docs reads, such as `status`, `tags` or `last_update`, a value of a type the build ignores.

title: fix: use dark-mode colours for the row rules of tables
description:
This PR fixes the horizontal rules of Markdown tables in dark mode. On every site, the rules between rows and along the bottom of a table stayed the light-mode grey, so they showed as bright lines next to the dark vertical rules. Their colour is fixed when the theme is compiled, and no dark-mode rule replaced it. Light mode is unchanged.

Before (dark mode):

![Table with bright horizontal rules in dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07710aca-964a-449a-8025-046f76bd0617)

After (dark mode):

![Table with all rules in the dark-mode border colour](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/366bcd54-d7fc-41ec-933d-944e17db5979)

title: refactor: render member summary tables as Markdown tables
description:
This PR writes the Methods, Attributes, Classes, Functions and Type aliases summary tables on reference pages as Quarto pipe tables instead of raw HTML. Pandoc reads a raw HTML table as one raw block per tag with paragraphs in between, so anything that works from the page's document tree, such as the planned move of Markdown companion pages into a Lua filter, cannot recover it as a table.

The tables keep their layout, fonts and links. Only their rules change colour, to match the other Markdown tables on the site: in light mode the bottom rule is light grey instead of near-black, and in dark mode the top rule and row separators use the dark-mode border colour instead of light grey. The hidden header row now follows the site language, because a Markdown copy of the page shows it.

Before (dark mode):

![Methods table with light grey rules in dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7f2feef-a327-49c6-9dd3-55d904076f30)

After (dark mode):

![Methods table with dark-mode rules](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/134f4b03-cf90-4740-bdac-d35019d3dd9f)

title: refactor: style the reference sidebar from the stylesheet
description:
This PR drops the `gd-ref-sidebar` class that the post-render script added to every page under `reference/`, and the inline styles it wrote onto the API and CLI Index links. Reference pages already carry the `doc-reference` or `doc-api-page` body class, so the stylesheet and the sidebar and keyboard scripts now key on those. Custom CSS that targeted `gd-ref-sidebar` should do the same.

The typing-information page and the fallback pages of versioned builds had no reference class, and now have one. The MCP Index link gets the same spacing as the API and CLI Index links. On reference pages the sidebar's line-breaking pass now changes only the sidebar, where it used to rewrite every menu label on the page, the navbar included.

title: fix: keep sidebar sections open without rewriting the HTML
description:
This PR stops the post-render script from stripping Quarto's collapse markup from every sidebar. The stylesheet already keeps every section open and hides the chevrons, and the sidebar script now removes the collapse attributes from section headings on every page, not only on reference pages.

It also fixes the navbar menu button and the sidebar toggle on API reference pages narrower than 992 px, which did nothing when tapped. On those pages the script removed collapse attributes from the whole page rather than only from the sidebar.

title: fix: load site scripts on nested pages without post-processing
description:
This PR writes the paths of the scripts Great Docs ships as root-relative (`/tooltips.js`), which Quarto rewrites for each page. They used to be bare relative paths, which only load on pages at the site root, so the post-render script rewrote a hardcoded list of about 20 script tags on every deeper page. A script added without also extending that list failed to load below the root.

Every page loads the same scripts as before.

title: feat: write the latest release into the navbar configuration
description:
This PR writes the navbar's release information into the generated Quarto configuration instead of injecting it after rendering. On a site with a text title, the version badge is now part of the navbar title. On a site whose navbar shows only a logo, the version and release date reach the logo's tooltip through a header meta tag.

The badge's hover text now follows the site language, as the logo tooltip already did. Pages whose content mentioned the badge, such as the changelog, were skipped and now show it. A malformed response from the GitHub releases API no longer stops the build of a site with a changelog.

title: fix: render the GitHub navbar widget without escaping its HTML
description:
This PR builds the GitHub navbar widget so that Quarto leaves its HTML intact. Quarto escapes the text of a navbar item that has no link, so the widget arrived on every page as literal text and the post-render script restored it with a regular expression. The widget entry now links to the repository, and Quarto keeps inline HTML in the text of a linked item.

With the widget inside a navbar link, the sidebar script erased it on API reference pages, because it rewrites every navigation label there. The widget script now takes the widget out of the link before building it, which also stops a click on the widget from following the link.

title: fix: hide empty footer sections with CSS
description: This PR replaces the post-render step that deleted empty footer sections with a stylesheet rule. Quarto writes all three footer sections and fills unconfigured ones with a non-breaking space, and on narrow screens each empty one took a full row below the footer text. The footer looks the same as before.

title: fix: label the search button without patching Quarto's files
description:
This PR moves two search fixes out of the post-render script. Every site showed two tooltips on the search button, one from Quarto's wrapper and one from the button itself. On sites in languages other than English the button also read "Search", because Quarto never passes its translated label to the autocomplete library, and post-render fixed that by editing Quarto's bundled `autocomplete.umd.js` in `_site/`.

The tooltip script now does both in the browser and leaves Quarto's files as shipped. The button also gets the translated label as its accessible name. When the search box had no placeholder, screen readers announced it as an unnamed button.

title: fix: hide page actions on the homepage without rewriting its HTML
description:
This PR stops the post-render script from deleting the page-actions script from the homepage and the API and CLI reference indexes. The reference indexes already carry a body class that the script skips, so only the generated homepage needed one, and the script now skips that too.

One thing changes for site authors. With `homepage: user_guide`, the first user-guide page becomes the homepage, and post-render stripped its Copy and View-as-Markdown buttons along with the generated homepage's. That page now keeps them, like every other user-guide page.

Before:

![Blended homepage without the page buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7e902ad-a898-4a71-aee7-90edec6b7433)

After:

![Blended homepage with the Copy page and Markdown buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4123d68-22c0-45d2-bf9f-203e71006248)

title: feat: write Markdown companions while Quarto renders pages
description:
This PR writes each page's `.md` companion from the page's own document while Quarto renders it. Before, the post-render step rebuilt the Markdown by converting the finished HTML, and the conversion lost content that readers and LLM tools expected to find.

The homepage, license and skills pages had no companion at all. Great Tables output and HTML tables with lists or rules in their cells did not come out as pipe tables, Mermaid diagrams lost their source, headings shifted level, and the homepage's companion included the sidebar of site links. Companions now keep all of these. Rendering a single page with the CLI now refreshes its companion too, and 404 and draft pages no longer get one.

title: fix: render long reference sidebars once instead of on every page
description:
Quarto rebuilds a page's whole sidebar on every page that shows it. On a large API this takes much of the render time: for a large API's reference sidebar it could list about 1,500 links, and every reference page has to render it. This PR has Quarto render each long reference sidebar once and then copies it into the pages that show it.

Before rendering, each reference sidebar (`reference`, `cli-reference`, `mcp-reference`) is copied to a full `gd-full-<id>` sidebar. Only a one-page template shows that copy, and the original sidebar keeps just the links the navbar needs, so Quarto renders a short sidebar on each page. After rendering, a post-render script (`share-sidebars.py`) takes the full sidebar from the template and puts it into each page. It marks the page's link as current, opens the sections around it, restores the search crumbs Quarto takes from the sidebar, and removes the template from the site and sitemap.

Pages aren't edited: the sidebar is named through the directory's `_metadata.yml`, so freeze caches stay valid. Normal builds run this just before rendering, and versioned builds run it in each version's directory.

The output matches a plain Quarto render: every page is byte-identical, and the search index holds the same entries. On a 303-page site with a 300-link reference sidebar, `quarto render` went from 241 to 145s (about 40% faster). Larger sidebars should save more. Sites with short sidebars (such as this one, with 14, 32 and 24 links) render in about the same time as before. A full versioned build of the Great Docs site succeeded, with the full sidebar and the right current link on the API, CLI and MCP pages in every version.

title: fix: refine the CLI reference: (1) full command names, (2) sections-driven listing, and (3) localized help summary
description:
This PR makes 3 fixes to the generated CLI reference. The CLI index now lists each command by its full invocation (e.g. `great-docs init` instead of `init`), matching the command page titles. When `cli.sections` is set, it now works like `reference.sections` does for the Python API: commands it doesn't list get no page, sidebar entry or index entry, so the sidebar and the index always agree.

The Great Docs site adds `check-examples` and `ci` to its sections so they stay documented, and a new "Grouping Commands" section in the user guide explains `cli.sections`. The "Full `--help` output" label on each command page now shows `--help` as monospace and is translated to all supported languages.

title: fix: keep llms.txt generation behind one shared guard
description:
# Summary

#350 points out that every page advertises `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, but
those files are only generated for projects that have an API reference. #351
gated the places that *advertise* the files on `_llms_txt_available()`, yet the
code that decides whether the files are actually written still had three
separate, slightly different opinions about when to run. This PR removes that
drift, so a page can never advertise a file the build will not write and a file
can never appear on disk without being advertised.

Two holes are closed:

- `_generate_llms_full_txt()` only required an `api-reference` block with a
  `package`, so a project with an empty `sections` list still got a
  header-only `llms-full.txt` written while `_llms_txt_available()` reported
  `False`. This is exactly the docs-only-site case from #350, where a page
  links a file that is effectively empty.
- `_prepare_for_freeze()` called `_generate_llms_txt()` and
  `_generate_llms_full_txt()` directly, bypassing the predicate `build()` gates
  on. The freeze path could therefore leave files behind that a full `build()`
  never writes, which breaks the invariant `_prepare_for_freeze` documents:
  that the build directory ends up holding files in exactly the state a full
  `build()` would produce.

Changes:

- New `_llms_txt_quarto_config()` is the single source of truth for the
  structural half of the guard: `_quarto.yml` exists, parses to a mapping, and
  its `api-reference` block has a `package` and at least one section. It
  returns the parsed config, or `None` when the project is not eligible.
- `_llms_txt_available()` delegates to that helper and keeps the importability
  check that only it needs.
- `_generate_llms_txt()` and `_generate_llms_full_txt()` use the same helper
  instead of re-parsing `_quarto.yml` under their own, narrower conditions.
- `_prepare_for_freeze()` now wraps both generator calls in
  `if self._llms_txt_available():`, so the freeze path and a full build agree.
- Tests parametrize six `_quarto.yml` shapes (no file, no `api-reference`, no
  sections, no package, unimportable package, importable package with
  sections) and assert that `_generate_llms_full_txt()` and
  `_prepare_for_freeze()` agree with `_llms_txt_available()` in every case.
  This extends the existing `test_llms_txt_available_matches_generators` from
  the predicate alone to the generators and the freeze path.

One deliberate scope note: `_generate_llms_txt()` is *not* given an
importability check. Existing tests such as `test_generate_llms_txt_writes_file`
and `test_generate_llms_txt_b9` pin the behaviour that it writes `llms.txt` for
a package that cannot be imported, and after this change both production call
sites (`build()` Step 3 and `_prepare_for_freeze()`) are gated by the predicate
anyway, so the asymmetry is no longer reachable in a real build. I would rather
flag it here than churn those tests in the same PR; happy to follow up if you
would prefer the guard moved into the generator itself.

- Ref: #350
- Follow-up to #351

# Verification

`pytest tests/test_great_docs.py -k "llms or margin or freeze"` passes with 94
tests. The full suite was run on Windows before and after the change: 7886
passed / 112 failed before, 7898 passed / 112 failed after, which is exactly the
12 new parametrized tests and no new failures. The 112 failures are pre-existing
and environment-specific (PTY recorder, layout migration, lint, skill install,
page status, interlinks) and reproduce identically on a clean checkout.
`ruff format` reports both files already formatted and `ruff check` adds no new

title: fix: name the Python reference section `python` in `ref_section_order:`
description:
The `ref_section_order:` option now names the Python reference section `python` instead of `api`, so the name will still be unambiguous once R or Rust reference docs arrive. `api` still works as an alias, so existing configs keep working, and repeated entries are now dropped. As before, sections a package doesn't have are skipped without an error, and the `gdtest_ref_section_order` test site now covers this by listing `mcp` for a package with no MCP server.

The Great Docs site itself now orders its reference sections as: CLI, Python, MCP.

title: fix: keep every member when expanding a module in reference contents
description:
# Summary

A bare module name in `reference:` contents expands to the module's public members. If the module contained a class, expansion stopped there, and the class and everything defined after it silently vanished from the docs.

`_CLASS_SUB_MAP` was assigned inside the top-level class branch of `_categorize_referenced_objects` but read in the module branch. Names are processed in `sorted()` order, so a module that sorted before any top-level class hit an `UnboundLocalError`. The `except Exception: pass` around the member loop swallowed it and ended the loop.

```text
_categorize_referenced_objects
  for name in sorted(top_level_names)
    class   -> binds _CLASS_SUB_MAP
    module  -> reads _CLASS_SUB_MAP     # unbound if no class sorted first
               except Exception: pass   # swallows UnboundLocalError, loop ends
```

The map had three identical inline copies, pasted in across three commits. This PR deletes them and defines the map once as a class attribute next to `_sub_classify_class`. There's no binding order left to get wrong.

```diff
 GreatDocs
   _ENUM_BASES
+  _CLASS_SUB_MAP
   _sub_classify_class
   _categorize_api_objects
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, top-level class branch
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, module-member branch
+    self._CLASS_SUB_MAP.get(...)        # both branches
   _categorize_referenced_objects
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, bound only in class branch
+    self._CLASS_SUB_MAP.get(...)        # class branch and module branch
```

`_categorize_api_objects` never had the bug. Its two lookups just switch to the shared attribute, so its behavior is unchanged.

# Evidence

- **Before** (new test against `main` at [79841694](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/tree/798416948ae42b9427b18a9ce1ac879c809792f4)):

  ```text
  FAILED tests/test_core.py::TestCategorizeReferencedObjects::test_module_expansion_without_top_level_class
  E   AssertionError: assert 'mymod.BDataclass' in []
  ```

  **After:**

  ```text
  tests/test_core.py: 253 passed
  ```
