title: refactor: move logo detection and favicon generation out of the build class
description:
Logo detection and favicon generation now live in the website package. Sites get the same logos and favicons as before.

The layout migration kept its own copy of the rules for where a logo may sit and how its dark variant is named. It now uses the build's rules. The two copies were identical, so migrations are unchanged.

title: refactor: move the project pages out of the build class
description:
The licence, citation, community and package-info pages are now written by their own modules. The generated pages are unchanged.

Their writers sat inside the homepage code in `core.py`: the four community pages (contributing guide, code of conduct, security policy, roadmap) were near-identical copies inside the method that builds the homepage's metadata margin, and the licence and citation pages inside the README conversion. The community pages now share one writer, and the package-info page gets its PyPI release dates from the build's remote source, which tests can stub.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move link checking out of the build class
description:
Link checking now lives in its own module, next to the other source checks. `GreatDocs.check_links` keeps its signature and results, and `great-docs check-links` prints the same output.

The method held URL extraction, HTTP probing and reporting in one 300-line body in `core.py`, mixed with the code that finds the package's modules and documentation pages, so the checker could only be tested through the build class.

One behaviour changes with the move. Link checking used to turn any error into an unreadable-file warning or a broken link. It now reports only a file it cannot read or a request that fails; any other error stops the check, so a bug in the checker no longer shows up as a broken link.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: escape the license name in the landing page license badge
description: The license badge in the Community section of the landing page now renders for every license. Some full license names contain double quotes, such as BSD-3-Clause's `BSD 3-Clause "New" or "Revised" License`. For those, the name ended the badge's tooltip attribute early, so Pandoc treated the tag as text and the landing page showed raw HTML instead of the badge.

title: refactor: group private modules into subpackages
description:
Ten private modules move from the top of the package into subpackages by concern, so the top level keeps the public modules and those many parts share. Proofreading, the Harper interface, linting and example checks go into `_checks/`; the MCP server reference and its launcher into `_mcpref/`; the version model and the versioned build into `_versions/`; and the build log and parallel rendering join `_build/`. Behaviour is unchanged.

The launcher the MCP reference starts in a subprocess now runs as `python -m great_docs._mcpref.runner`. Strict pyright covers the new packages; the six moved modules that do not pass it yet sit on its `exclude` list, and removing a line makes that module strict.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move the `freeze:` and metadata page passes into the website package
description:
The two passes that rewrite page sources just before Quarto renders, expanding a page's `freeze:` shorthand and writing search descriptions and social card tags, now live in one module of the website package. The versioned build had its own copy of the metadata pass, which read `_quarto.yml` differently; both builds now call the same function, and no page's output changes.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move `llms.txt` generation into the website package
description:
The `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` writers now live in their own module in the website package. They used to be nine methods on `GreatDocs`, and each reached back into the class for the package metadata, the Click CLI and the user guide; the build step now gathers those and passes them in.

One fix comes with the move. `llms-full.txt` dropped a user guide page's front matter by splitting at the first two `---` it found, so a title such as "Before --- after" leaked the rest of the front matter into the file. The front matter now ends at its closing line, as Quarto reads it.

Errors raised by the documented package while reading summaries and signatures are now limited to the errors importing user code can raise; any other error stops the step instead of being hidden. No generated Quarto project changes. Four test cases record the same handled `ValueError` at its handler's new location, so this PR goes without the strict project-diff check.

title: fix!: make `GreatDocs.proofread` check files as `great-docs proofread` does
description:
`GreatDocs.proofread` now checks files the way `great-docs proofread` does. The method had its own copy of the proofreading pipeline, which the command never used: it sent whole Quarto pages, front matter and code blocks included, to Harper without the built-in dictionary or the default ignored rules, so it reported far more issues than the command. Both now share one engine.

The method's interface changes to match the user guide. Extra words go in `custom_words` (it was `custom_dictionary`), `strict=True` checks with every rule and no built-in dictionary, and the result is a list of checked files, each with `file`, `issues` and `error`, instead of a dictionary of counts. A missing `harper-cli` raises `RuntimeError` for the whole run.

`great-docs proofread --include-docstrings` with no listed files now checks the package's Python files. Before, it found only the documentation pages, so the flag did nothing.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move export discovery and init-time probes out of the build class
description:
Export discovery, the sorting of exports into reference sections, and the probes `great-docs init` runs to choose `parser` and `dynamic` now live in a private reference package and work from a package griffe has already loaded. `great-docs scan`, the MCP server and `great-docs lint` call the same code, and lint now loads the package once per run.

Two fixes come with the move, both for a package that cannot be imported, for example because a dependency is missing. The reference listed each of its classes with no methods and said nothing; it now warns once and keeps the methods griffe's static analysis finds. `great-docs init` wrote `dynamic: true` for such a package, although dynamic mode imports every documented object; it now warns, suggests installing the dependencies, and writes `dynamic: false`. The dynamic-mode probe also samples the package's exports instead of the first names in `__init__.py`, which were often its own imports.

An error that importing user code cannot raise now stops the command instead of filing an export under Other.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: file subclasses of a package's own exceptions under exceptions
description:
API reference sections and the badges on reference pages now classify objects with one set of rules. They used to keep separate copies that disagreed, so an object could be listed in one section while its page labelled it as something else:

- `class MyErr(Err)`, where `Err` subclasses `ValueError` in the same package, was filed as a class.
- `T = TypeVar("T")` and `X: TypeAlias = ...` were listed under Constants.
- Subclasses of `ExceptionGroup`, `EncodingWarning` and three other built-in exceptions missing from a hand-written list were filed as classes.

In the Gauntlet this moves objects between sections in `gdtest_exceptions`, `gdtest_type_aliases` and `gdtest_complete_docstrings`.

title: refactor: group the remaining top-level private modules into subpackages
description:
This PR moves ten private modules out of the top level of `great_docs` and into the subpackage that owns each one's concern, and deletes one module that nothing imports. Site authors and readers see no change.

Each of these modules served a single area of the code but sat beside the modules that every part of the package uses, so the top level no longer showed which modules were shared. The Go and Rust command-line extractors now sit with the Click extractor in the CLI reference package. The root-layout notice joins the layout migration package. The d2, mock-code and Mermaid page passes and the SPDX licence data join the website package. The three table preview modules form a new `_tables` package, and the `tbl-preview` and `tbl-explorer` shortcodes import them from there. The unused git history helpers are gone.

title: fix: check the authored pages the build publishes
description:
`great-docs check-links` and `great-docs proofread` now check the same pages as `great-docs lint`: the homepage, the user guide, each section and each custom pages directory, plus the package's `README.md`.

Before, both commands read little more than the user guide. Pages in sections and custom pages directories went unchecked. The homepage was missed unless it was the `README.md`. A project without a user guide had its generated build directory link-checked instead, reference pages included. Proofreading also read a `recipes/` directory even when no section published it. Include files whose names start with `_` are no longer checked on their own, since Quarto doesn't render them. Docstrings and source files are now found in `src/`, `python/` and `lib/` package layouts, which both commands missed before.

The build and `lint` also stop warning about a missing `custom/` directory in projects that never configured custom pages. Internally, the custom pages code moves out of `GreatDocs` into its own module, with no change to the built site.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move the user guide into its own module and fix its navbar link
description:
The user guide's discovery, page copying and sidebar generation move out of `core.py` into a module of their own, and a build now finds the guide once. Each step that needed the guide used to search for it again and repeat its warnings, so a missing configured directory or a missing listed page was reported several times; those warnings now print once, under "Prepare build directory".

Three fixes come with the move. The User Guide navbar link pointed at `user-guide/index.qmd` whenever an explicit guide listed an `index.qmd`, a page that does not exist when that file sits in a subdirectory; the link now points at the guide's first published page. A guide directory with no pages no longer causes links into it to be rewritten to `user-guide/...` pages the build never publishes. And `great-docs check-links`, `great-docs proofread`, `great-docs freeze --info` and the MCP server's add-page tool now read the guide from the directory the build uses (a configured `user_guide` path, or `user-guide/`), not only from `user_guide/`.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: move CLI discovery and reference pages into one package
description:
The code that finds a package's Click or Typer command line, writes its CLI reference pages and records it in API snapshots now lives in one private package. Before, it was spread across the documentation builder, a Typer module and a separate copy in the API comparison code. The reference pages are unchanged.

The API snapshot saved after a build used its own copy of CLI discovery, so it could describe a different command from the reference pages. It now follows the pages' rules: with `cli.module` unset it also searches the package's `console` and `commands` modules, and when `cli.name` names something that is not a command it records no CLI rather than picking another command from the module.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: write the sitemap, robots file and metadata partial from the website package
description:
The code that writes `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` and the HTML metadata partial now lives beside the other SEO and website features instead of in the documentation builder. Built sites are unchanged, and the build and `great-docs seo --fix` print the same lines as before.

These writers printed their own messages and each looked up the site's canonical address, which tied them to the builder. They now take the address from their caller and report through a callback, so the build and the `seo` command share them directly.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: write README and blended homepages through one page writer
description:
The README homepage and the homepage promoted from the first user guide page (`homepage: user_guide`) are now written by one page writer, instead of two builder methods that each assembled the front matter, hero and sidebar. The written pages are unchanged: the README homepage keeps its sidebar in Quarto's margin column, and the user guide homepage keeps it after the body, where a margin column would shift the guide's grid and mobile readers see the content first.

A README homepage with `hero.name: true` no longer stops the build with an `AttributeError`; it now builds and keeps the README's title.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: remove the documented-symbol queries from GreatDocs
description:
The public `GreatDocs.documented_symbol_names` and `GreatDocs.documented_objects` methods are removed, without a deprecation period since Great Docs is pre-1.0. `api-snapshot`, `api-diff --graph` and `lint` now read the documented symbols through the same reference code the build uses. A versioned build no longer creates a separate documentation project for each version whose API snapshot is not cached; it lists the working tree's documented symbols once per build.

The list now also respects `reference: false` and projects without Python. Before, it still discovered the package's exports for such sites, so API snapshots, `api-diff --graph` and lint's cross-reference checks described an API the site does not publish.

title: fix: read section `versions:` as expressions and drop navbar links to excluded sections
description:
This lands #562 and #567 on `main`. Both were approved and merged, but into the stack branch below them after that branch had already merged, so their changes never reached `main`. The commits here are the same ones, unchanged.

A section's `versions:` setting now accepts the same values as page front matter: a tag, a version expression such as `">=0.5"`, or a list of either. Before, a string was tested as a substring of the tag being built. And a section that `versions:` leaves out of a version now loses its navbar links in that version too, instead of linking readers to a missing page.

title: fix: name the CLI after its script and show choices, deprecation and argument help
description:
This lands #564 and #566 on `main`. Both were approved and merged, but into the stack branch below them after that branch had already merged, so their changes never reached `main`. The commits here are the same ones, unchanged.

When `pyproject.toml` lists several scripts, the CLI reference now names the command after the script that runs it, not the first one listed. CLI reference pages also show the accepted values of a `click.Choice` instead of `CHOICE`, mark deprecated commands, options and arguments, and include argument help.

title: fix: drop navbar links to sections a version excludes
description:
On a versioned site, a section that its `versions:` setting leaves out of a version now loses its navbar link in that version too.

Before, the versioned build removed the section's pages and sidebar entries from the excluded version but kept its navbar link, so readers of the older version clicked through to a missing page. The build now removes navbar links into the section from both sides of the navbar and from menus, and drops a menu left empty. Versions that include the section keep their navbar unchanged.

Stacked on #562; merge #557 and #562 first.

title: fix: show choices, deprecation and argument help in the CLI reference
description:
CLI reference pages now show the accepted values of a `click.Choice`, mark deprecated commands, options and arguments, and include argument help. The command line declared all three, but the pages dropped them.

A `Choice` option or argument showed its type as `CHOICE`; it now lists the values in Click's notation, such as `[json|yaml|toml]`, which changes Great Docs' own CLI reference. A deprecated command, option or argument looked like any other: a deprecated command now gets a warning callout under its description, as deprecated API objects do, and a deprecated option or argument has its help led by a bold "Deprecated." with Click's message, without Click's own "(DEPRECATED)" suffix repeating it. Argument help, which clap command lines give for positional arguments, was extracted but never shown; it now follows "Required." or "Optional." as option help does.

Stacked on #564; merge #555 and #564 first.

title: test: fail tests that reach the network
description:
The test suite now fails any test that looks up or connects to a host other than this machine, and the failure names the host. This is for maintainers: no site output changes.

A run with outbound connections refused found twelve core tests and one synthetic test that reached the network: nine through the build's GitHub API requests, one link-checker test against `httpbin.org`, and two that made DNS lookups for domains that don't exist. Their results depended on the network being up, and a CI run without network access, or a GitHub rate limit, could fail them.

Those tests now use preset GitHub data or a fake HTTP response. A test that genuinely needs the network opts out with the new `network` marker; only the live skill-install integration test uses it. The guard covers the test process only, so builds and Quarto renders run in subprocesses are unaffected.

title: fix: name the CLI after the script that runs the documented command
description:
When `pyproject.toml` lists several scripts, the CLI reference now names the command after the script that actually runs it, rather than whichever script comes first.

Before, a package with `scripts = { helper = "pkg.tools:main", pkg = "pkg.cli:cli" }` documented the `pkg.cli` command but called it `helper` throughout its CLI pages and in `llms.txt`. The name came from the first `[project.scripts]` entry, with no check of what that script runs.

Great Docs now picks the script whose entry point names the documented Click command or Typer app, and falls back to the first script only when none does, for example when a script calls a wrapper function. The CLI documentation guide describes the rule.

Stacked on #555; merge that first.

title: feat: group a section's card index the way its sidebar groups pages
description:
The generated card index and the sidebar were two views of the same section, and they did not agree. The sidebar grouped pages by subdirectory. The index ignored those groups, put every page with an image in one grid, and dropped pages without an image into a list under a horizontal rule.

When a section has subdirectory groups, or `sidebar_groups` is set, the generated index now uses those same groups, titles, and order. Each group is a Markdown heading and one `.section-cards` grid. A page without an image stays in its group. Top-level pages stay in one grid before the first heading. Pages that `sidebar_groups` does not name stay after the groups, with no heading. A section with no groups keeps the flat image-then-plain layout. `index_groups: false` keeps that layout even when the sidebar has groups. A hand-written `index.qmd` is still used as-is.

The headings are Markdown, so a site that shows a table of contents will list them. The card markup is unchanged.

Fixes #553.

title: fix: read a section's `versions:` as a version expression
description:
A section's `versions:` setting now accepts the same values as page front matter: a tag, a version expression such as `">=0.5"`, or a list of either.

Before, a string value was tested as a substring of the tag being built, so `versions: ">=0.5"` dropped the section from 0.6 and kept it in 0.5 only by accident. Page-level `versions:` already read expressions, so the two settings behaved differently for the same value. List entries now resolve the way page entries do, so a `v`-prefixed tag also matches.

```{.yaml filename="great-docs.yml"}
sections:
  - title: Migrations
    dir: migrations
    versions: ">=0.5"   # this version and every newer one
```

Stacked on #557; merge that first.

title: fix: keep the blended homepage's front matter whole when a value holds `---`
description:
A blended homepage (`homepage: user_guide`) now keeps its front matter intact when a value contains `---`, such as a title `A---B`.

The blended homepage promotes the first user guide page to the site's index. It found that page's front matter by splitting on the first two `---` anywhere in the text, so a title containing `---` cut the block short: the homepage lost its title, and the rest of the front matter appeared as text at the top of the page. It now ends the front matter at the first line that starts with `---`, as every other page does.

This was the last place that located front matter by splitting on `---`; the other readers already use the shared, line-anchored rule.

title: fix: match a section's `versions:` scoping to its published directory
description:
On a versioned site, a section whose `versions:` list leaves out a version is now removed from that version whatever its `dir:` looks like.

The versioned build recognised a section only when its `dir:` was a single directory name spelt exactly as published. A nested `dir: guides/migrations`, or `dir: Migration_Guides` (published as `migration-guides/`), stayed in every version, so readers of an older version saw pages the author had scoped out. Matching on single path components also removed unrelated pages: a `recipes` section took `user-guide/recipes/` with it.

The build now locates each section where the site publishes it, using the same naming as the section's pages and navbar link. The first commit makes the project layout a required argument of the versioned build, deleting a fallback that only tests used, so the fix can rely on it.

title: fix: warn when a CLI module exists but fails to import
description:
Site authors whose CLI module fails to import now see a warning in the normal build output that names the module and the error. Before, the CLI reference was silently missing.

When `cli.module` is not set, great-docs looks for the command line in the package's `cli`, `__main__`, `main`, `console` and `commands` modules. A module that existed but failed to import, for example because it imports a dependency that is not installed, was treated as if it did not exist. The build reported "No Click CLI found" only in its detailed output, so the site lost its CLI pages with no visible sign of why.

Now only a module that is genuinely absent is skipped. `llms-full.txt` is still written, without the CLI, and the warning appears once.

title: fix: translate the whole Skills page intro in every language
description:
On a non-English site, the Skills page now opens with a complete translated paragraph in all three of its forms.

Before, each form was broken outside English. A site with several skills showed the raw key `skills_intro_multi` where the intro should be, because no translation existed for it. A generated skill's page showed only the first sentence of the paragraph, and a curated skill's page showed only the last, which began with a pronoun that referred to nothing; in French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and Polish that pronoun also had the wrong grammatical gender.

Each form is now one paragraph translated as a whole for all 25 languages: what a skill is, where this page's skill came from or how to switch between skills, and what installing one does. English pages are unchanged.

title: fix: keep an authored homepage source's front matter on the homepage
description:
A homepage built from an authored `index.qmd`, `index.md` or README now keeps all of the source's front matter, so options such as `execute:`, `page-layout:`, `format:` and `css:` take effect on the homepage.

Before, the homepage kept only the source's title and description. Everything else was silently dropped, so an author who set `page-layout: full` or `execute: echo: false` in `index.qmd` saw the default layout and visible code on the rendered homepage, with no warning.

The homepage still turns off the table of contents and adds its own `gd-homepage` class, but an authored `toc:` now wins, and authored `body-classes:` are kept alongside `gd-homepage` rather than replaced. A source with only a title and description renders exactly as before. The configuration guide gains a short "Homepage Front Matter" section.

title: fix: publish the companion files the Skills page shows
description:
A skill's companion files are now chosen by one rule, so the Skills page and the published `.well-known/agent-skills/` copy always list the same files.

A single skill, set by `skill.file` or found in `skills/<package>/`, showed its companion files on the Skills page but published only `SKILL.md`, so an agent following the page could not fetch them. The page and multi-skill publishing also disagreed: the page showed only text files directly inside `references/`, `scripts/` and `assets/`, while multi-skill mode published every file in the skill's directory, as the user guide documents. And a `skill.file: SKILL.md` at the project root pulled the project's own `assets/` onto the page.

Now every file under the skill's directory, except `SKILL.md` and hidden files, is a companion file in every mode: published, listed in `index.json` and in the page's layout tree, with the text files shown in full. A skill whose `SKILL.md` sits in the project root or the docs directory has no companion files. Multi-skill sites no longer publish hidden files from a skill's directory.

title: fix: give a sidebar to a section whose pages share one subdirectory
description:
A custom section whose pages all sit in one subdirectory now gets a sidebar listing them, with the subdirectory as a titled group.

Before, such a section (for example `dir: guides` holding only `guides/advanced/*.qmd`) got neither a sidebar nor the `gd-section-no-sidebar` body class. The sidebar counted the subdirectory as a single item and was dropped, while the full-width class was kept for sections of at most one page. Readers saw the narrow layout with an empty space where the sidebar should be, and no way to move between the section's pages.

Both decisions now count pages, including the index, so every section gets exactly one of the two. A section whose `sidebar_groups` put every page in one group had the same bug and is fixed too.

title: fix: read every static `__all__` form when export discovery falls back
description:
When great-docs cannot find a package's exports by static analysis, it falls back to reading `__all__` from the package's `__init__.py`. That fallback understood only a single `__all__ = [...]` list. A package that built `__all__` from tuples, `+` or `+=` was reported as having no `__all__`, and an assignment inside a function counted as if it ran at module level.

The fallback also applied only the `exclude` setting, not the automatic exclusions. So names such as `main`, `cli`, `version` and `logger`, which the normal discovery path leaves out, appeared in the API reference.

The fallback now reads module-level assignments in source order, accepting list and tuple literals, `+`, `+=` and annotated assignments, and applies the same automatic exclusions, `auto_include` and `no_auto_exclude` rules as the normal path.

title: fix: keep navbar ordering, placement and icons working on translated sites
description:
On a site whose `site.lang` is not English, Great Docs translated the labels of its own navbar items (User Guide, Recipes, Reference, Changelog and Tags) every time it wrote `_quarto.yml`, then looked the items up by their English label. On a French site, `navbar_order: [Reference, User Guide]` had no effect, a section with `navbar_after: Reference` did not follow "Référence", section links went last instead of before Reference, and an English `nav_icons` key put no icon on the translated item. A user's own item labelled "Reference" was translated too.

Great Docs now finds its own items by their link target and labels them in the site's language when it adds them, so a user's items keep the text they were given. `navbar_order`, `navbar_after` and the navbar keys of `nav_icons` accept the English or the translated label of those five items:

```yaml
site:
  lang: fr
navbar_order: [Reference, User Guide]  # or [Référence, Guide d'utilisation]
nav_icons:
  navbar:
    Reference: code-2                   # also reaches "Référence"
```

title: fix: list exports in `__all__` order and report listed names that discovery cannot find
description:
The API reference now lists a package's exports in the order its `__all__` gives them. Until now, each section followed the order of definition in the source, so an author who ordered `__all__` deliberately saw that order lost. The order also depended on the route: when griffe found none of the `__all__` names and great-docs read `__all__` itself, the reference already kept `__all__` order.

A name in `__all__` that static analysis cannot find, such as one a module `__getattr__` provides, is still left out of the reference. The build output now names it among the other excluded objects, as in `Excluding 1 object(s) (not found by static analysis): lazy_name`. Before, it was dropped without a word.

title: fix: refuse to replace output directories a remote build did not write
description:
`great-docs build --from-repo` no longer deletes an existing `--output-dir` unless that directory is empty or holds a site an earlier build copied there.

Before, the remote build removed whatever directory `--output-dir` named, then copied the site in. `--output-dir .` deleted the working directory, and pointing it at a project deleted the project. The default output path, the checkout's site directory under the working directory, had the same exposure. The local build already guards its deployment output with an ownership manifest that lists the files it wrote; the remote build now applies the same rule, checks it before installing and building so a refusal fails within seconds, and writes the manifest on the copied site:

- `--output-dir .` stops with `Error: Deployment directory is not Great Docs-generated output: /home/me/project` and leaves the directory untouched.
- A rerun to `./site` whose contents are unchanged replaces the old site.
- A rerun to `./site` after adding a file there stops with `Error: Deployment directory contains unrecognised content: /home/me/site/CNAME`.
- Output that a remote build wrote before this change has no manifest, so the first rerun to it stops with the first message. Remove it by hand once; later runs replace it.

title: fix: apply section-level versions scoping in versioned builds
description:
A multi-version site now leaves a section out of every version that its `versions:` list omits.

The multi-version guide documents a `versions:` list on a `sections:` entry, but the versioned build never read it, so every version published every section. With the configuration below, version 0.1 still published the migration guides, listed them in its sidebar and recorded them in the version map. Now only 0.2 and 0.3 carry them.

```yaml
sections:
  - title: Migration Guides
    dir: migrations
    versions: ["0.2", "0.3"]
```

title: fix: publish the MCP discovery manifest when skill discovery is off
description:
Sites that document an MCP server now serve `/.well-known/mcp.json` whatever the skill settings.

Great Docs writes the manifest into the build directory, but Quarto copies a hidden directory into the site only when `project.resources` lists it. The build listed `.well-known/` only for the skill discovery files, so a site with `skill.enabled: false` or `skill.well_known: false` built the manifest and never published it. Clients and registries that look for the server at the site's address found nothing.

title: fix: keep building when llms.txt or SKILL.md generation fails
description:
A site author whose package trips up the `llms.txt` or `SKILL.md` step now gets a warning in the build log and a finished site, instead of a build that stops at step 3 or 4.

Both steps import and inspect the user's package, as the CLI and MCP reference steps do. Those two steps report import, attribute, runtime and file errors as warnings and carry on, but the `llms.txt` and `SKILL.md` steps let the same errors end the build. With `cli.enabled: true`, for example, a command-line module that raised `RuntimeError` on import stopped the build in the `llms.txt` step, before the CLI reference step could report it as a warning.

title: fix: remove the duplicate README title whenever the homepage shows a hero
description:
A README homepage with a hero no longer shows the package name twice when the hero appears without `hero.enabled: true`.

The homepage drops a README's first heading when it repeats the name the hero shows. It did so only when `hero.enabled` was set, but the hero also turns on by itself when the site has a `logo-hero.*` image or the README opens with a centred logo or tagline block. On those sites the reader saw the package name in the hero and again as the first heading below it.

title: fix: escape the homepage hero and sidebar text written into HTML
description:
The homepage hero and metadata sidebar now show names, taglines, badges, logos, project links and author and funder details exactly as configured.

These values went into the page's HTML unchanged. A `<` in `hero.tagline`, the package description or an author's name was read as a tag, so text vanished from the page. A quote in a badge URL, a logo's `alt`, or an author's `homepage` ended the attribute early, so the link pointed somewhere else. The package-info page already escaped values of this kind. Values without `<`, `>`, `&` or quotes render as before.

title: fix: keep building when a CLI module exits on import
description:
A package's `__main__.py` no longer ends the build. When a package has no `cli.py`, CLI discovery imports its `__main__.py`. If that file calls its command without an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard, the command runs, Click parses the build's own arguments, prints a usage error and exits, and the build stops with that exit status.

Discovery now treats an import that exits as a failed import and tries the next candidate module. With `cli.module` set to such a module, the build reports that importing it exited and carries on without CLI pages. The API diff stopped the same way when it snapshotted the CLI of such a release. It now records no CLI commands for that release.

title: fix: escape CLI reference values and write the pages as UTF-8
description:
CLI reference pages now show option values containing `<`, `>` or `&`, accept a `cli.title` with a double quote, and build on non-UTF-8 locales.

Option and argument names, types and defaults went into the page HTML unescaped, so a default such as `<stdin>` vanished as an unknown tag. So did the value names of Rust (clap) options: `-c, --config <PATH>` showed as `-c, --config`, and now shows in full. A `cli.title` containing `"` broke the index page's front matter, and the pages were written in the locale's encoding, so help text with `•` failed the build under cp1252 on Windows.

title: fix: leave unindexed pages, redirect stubs and older versions out of the sitemap
description:
`sitemap.xml` no longer lists pages that search engines should not index.

The sitemap left out only paths that start with `_` or `.`, so it also listed pages with a `noindex` robots directive, such as `skills.html`, and redirect stubs: the `v/latest/`, `v/stable/` and `v/dev/` aliases of a versioned site and the pages Quarto writes for `aliases:` front matter. In a site with `versions`, it listed every page of the older versions under `v/` too, although their canonical links point at the latest version. The sitemap now skips all three. A site without `versions` keeps any `v/` directory in its sitemap.

title: fix: keep a page's execute options when expanding its freeze shorthand
description:
Pages that set `freeze:` at the top of their front matter now keep their other `execute` options. Great Docs moves the shorthand under `execute:`, where Quarto reads it, but it recognised only a block-style `execute:`. A page with a flow-style mapping, such as

```yaml
freeze: auto
execute: {echo: false}
```

got a second `execute:` key, and because the last duplicate wins, `echo: false` was silently dropped. The shorthand now joins the existing mapping in either style, and a `freeze` already set under `execute:` takes precedence.

title: fix: publish skill.md when the first listed skill is skipped
description: Sites that list their skills under `skill.skills` now always publish `skill.md`. It was copied only from the first entry, so when that entry was skipped (no `name` or `file`, or a file that does not exist), the site had no `skill.md` while the Skills page still pointed its install command, agent prompt and raw link at it. The first skill that is actually published now becomes `skill.md`, which is also the skill the page shows first.

title: fix: proofread .qmd pages given by a relative path
description: `great-docs proofread` now checks `.qmd` pages given by a path relative to the working directory. `great-docs proofread user_guide/a.qmd`, the form the command's own help shows, exited with "is not in the subpath of", and so did `--docs-dir` whenever the directory held a `.qmd` page; `.md` and `.py` files were unaffected. A page outside the project is now reported by the path it was given.

title: fix: stop the homepage repeating README text around centred badge blocks
description:
The homepage now takes badges from a README's `<div align="center">` block reliably. Two layouts went wrong. When a closed centred block was followed later by an unclosed one holding badges, the README text between the two appeared twice on the homepage. When a centred block contained a nested `<div>`, for example around its logo, it was taken to end at the inner closing tag, so the badges and logo after it were missed and the whole block stayed in the homepage body.

A centred block is now read up to its own closing tag, and one that never closes is left in place.

title: fix: make tag pills open the tags page at their tag's heading
description:
Clicking a tag pill on a page now opens the tags page at that tag's heading. The headings on the tags page carried no `id`, so on any site with `tags.enabled: true` every pill linked to an anchor that did not exist, and the browser opened the tags page at the top.

The build now chooses each heading's id and hands it to the pills, so the two always agree, nested tags and their parents included. Tags with non-ASCII letters, such as `Données`, now get a working anchor, and tags that would share one, such as `C++` and `C`, get distinct ones.

title: refactor: assemble the site-wide Quarto settings in one ordered function
description:
This PR moves the steps that merge Great Docs' site-wide settings into `_quarto.yml` out of the build class and into a single function that applies them in a fixed order. The build step now only gathers the inputs, such as the GitHub repository, package metadata and the site's identity, then calls it. The generated configuration is unchanged. One printed line moves: on the first pass, a warning about fetching GitHub data now appears before the line naming the bibliography files.

Before, the order of these settings lived in a long method on `GreatDocs`, mixed with the code that gathered their inputs. That order matters: later settings read entries that earlier ones add, and it fixes the order in which pages load scripts and stylesheets. The writes to `_quarto.yml` also still took the Great Docs configuration, although they stopped using it once navbar labels were translated when the items are made, so this PR drops that parameter.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: configure the site's appearance and navigation icons in their own modules
description:
The site's appearance features now configure themselves in their own modules: the wide layout toggle, announcement banner, navbar and content styles, accent and navbar colours, scale-to-fit selectors and navigation icons. Their code was about 440 lines inside the method that builds `_quarto.yml`, which made each feature hard to find and test on its own.

This also fixes the order of two styles. With `accent_color` or `navbar_color` set together with `content_style`, the second configuration pass moved the colour styles from before the content style script to after it. Each entry is now replaced where it stands.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: add project resources and render exclusions through contributions
description:
Build steps now return the files Quarto should copy into the site, and the files it should not render, as part of their contribution. Before, the main build class edited `project.resources` and `project.render` itself, in a long block for the fixed resources and in a helper that custom pages and terminal recordings each called. A step therefore could not say what it added to the site without the build class.

The fixed resources live in one website module: marimo notebooks, asset directories, `assets/`, `_shared/` and the skill files. A `project.render: null` in an existing configuration no longer raises an error.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: keep the build's includes when a site lists its own
description:
A `site:` list for `include-in-header`, `include-before-body` or `include-after-body` in `great-docs.yml` now follows the includes Great Docs writes instead of replacing them. The build updates the Quarto configuration twice, and the list replaced the build's entries on the second update. That erased the page tag and status data, so tag pills and status badges rendered without data.

The site's own `.scss` and `.css` files in `site.theme` now override Great Docs' styles. Great Docs' stylesheet goes after the Bootswatch theme and before the site's files, so `[cosmo, custom.scss]` becomes `[cosmo, great-docs.scss, custom.scss]`. Before, Great Docs' stylesheet came last and overrode them.

The Quarto project defaults and the `site` passthrough also move out of `core.py` into their own module.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: offer only the references a site has in the reference switcher
description:
The reference switcher now lists the CLI and MCP references only when the build wrote their pages. Before, it listed the CLI reference whenever a Click, Go or Rust CLI was enabled, even when the build found no CLI and wrote no CLI pages.

Its script is now copied into a site only when the site shows the switcher, and is then listed in `project.resources`. Before, every site with a CLI or MCP reference enabled got a copy, which includes every site under the default `mcp` setting.

The switcher's configuration also moves out of `core.py` into its own module. This removes the separate step that edited the written `_quarto.yml` to drop the MCP section when the MCP server was missing or failed.

title: refactor: add the version selector before writing the Quarto configuration
description:
A versioned site's version map, warning-banner setting and selector script are now added to the Quarto configuration in memory, before the build writes it. They used to be added by reading the written `_quarto.yml` back, editing it and writing it a second time. The generated configuration is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: write the page footer from its own module
description:
The page footer, the Great Docs attribution and the "Supported by Posit" badge are now written by their own website module instead of inline in the Quarto configuration step, at the same point in the build, so the generated configuration is unchanged.

The attribution's lookup of the Great Docs commit used to catch every exception, which could hide a real error behind a missing commit link. It now catches only a missing or failing `git` and its timeout.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: build the navbar brand from GitHub data fetched once per build
description:
The site title, logo, favicons, GitHub entry and latest-release badge are now set by one navigation module instead of inline in the long Quarto configuration step. That step runs twice per build, and each run fetched the repository's star and fork counts and its latest release again. A build now fetches them once and reuses them on the second run, so it makes half as many GitHub requests.

The branch also fixes a configured `favicon` being ignored when the site had no logo. The favicon is now generated and linked from every page whether or not a logo is configured or found.

title: refactor: return the CLI and MCP reference sidebars as contributions
description:
The CLI and MCP reference steps now return their sidebars, and the CLI reference's navbar link, as a contribution that is applied to the Quarto configuration, as the changelog and tags steps already do. Each step used to edit `_quarto.yml` itself with its own rules for finding sidebars and navbar items, including lookups by English label.

A navbar link from a build step is now skipped when the navbar already has an item for the same Great Docs destination, such as the API reference's Reference item, not only when an item has the same target. The CLI sidebar step also no longer adds an "API Index" link that the API reference already puts first, a check that raised `TypeError` on one sidebar shape. Every build writes the same configuration as before.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: resolve the site name and addresses in one place
description:
This PR gathers the site name, the configured site URL and the preferred address for canonical links into one value, built from the configuration, the repository and the generated `_quarto.yml`. Page titles, social cards, structured data, raw custom pages and `great-docs seo` used to ask the build object for each value through separate methods, each of which detected the repository again. Copying the default social card image into the site now lives with the rest of the social card code. No output changes.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: copy and list each site script only where pages load it
description:
Great Docs decided which of its site-root scripts a site gets in three separate lists: one for copying files into the build directory, one for `project.resources` and one for the page includes. The lists disagreed, so `github-widget.js`, `sidebar-filter.js` and `dark-mode-toggle.js` were copied into every site and listed as resources even when no page loaded them. One table now drives all three, which also removes the repeated list-editing code from the Quarto configuration step.

Sites without a GitHub repository, or with the sidebar filter or dark-mode toggle turned off, no longer publish those unused files, and `project.resources` lists the scripts in the order pages load them. What pages load, and in what order, does not change.

title: refactor: share package-name detection between build and layout migration
description:
The build and the layout migration each had their own code for choosing the package name used in name-specific logo candidates such as `<name>_logo.svg`. The copies applied the same rule, but could drift apart and make the migration look for a different logo than the build.

Both now use one function: the declared distribution name wins, then the sole package directory at the project root. Behaviour is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: stop looking for a logo in docs/assets below the configuration
description:
Navbar logo detection no longer treats `docs/assets/logo.svg` and `docs/assets/logo.png` as candidates. Logo paths are relative to the directory holding `great-docs.yml`, so with the configuration in `docs/` those candidates pointed at `docs/docs/assets/` and could never match.

A project with `great-docs.yml` in `docs/` still finds `docs/assets/logo.svg` as `assets/logo.svg`. A project with `great-docs.yml` at the root that keeps its logo in `docs/assets/` no longer gets it detected, and needs the setting:

```yaml
logo: docs/assets/logo.svg
```

title: fix: name the package on the citation page
description:
The introduction on the authors and citation page now names the project, as in "To cite great-docs in publications, please use the following citation." It used to say "To cite this package in publications" on every site.

The page was meant to read the name from the build's metadata, but that never held a name, so the fallback always won. The page now takes the project's distribution name directly. Sites with no detectable name keep "this package".

title: fix: use forward slashes in tag page links on Windows
description:
On Windows, the links on tag pages and the page keys in the tag and page-status data for the user guide, recipes and custom sections held backslashes, such as `user-guide\advanced\intro.qmd`. The paths came from the operating system's separator, so the links did not resolve on the built site.

These paths now always use `/`. Builds on macOS and Linux are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: escape the package-info page title in its front matter
description:
A package-info page whose title contains a double quote, such as a translated title, produced invalid YAML front matter, so Quarto failed to read the page. The title was written between double quotes without escaping.

The front matter is now serialised as YAML, which quotes a value only when it needs quoting. Titles with quotes or colons round-trip, and an ordinary title is written as `title: Package Info` rather than `title: "Package Info"`. The rendered page is the same.

title: refactor: derive each version's site configuration in memory
description:
This stops a versioned build from writing the prepared configuration to `_quarto.yml` and reading it back for every version. Each version's configuration is now derived from a separate copy of the prepared mapping, so a version's build directory, the latest included, receives two writes: the initial configuration that marks it as generated, then its own.

Watch mode and `great-docs freeze` still write the prepared configuration at the end of preparation, because they render the build directory's file directly. When `--versions` selects only older versions, the build directory keeps the initial configuration, which is neither read nor rendered. Generated sites are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: record step changes as contributions applied by the configuration step
description:
This stops a dozen preparation steps from each reading and rewriting `_quarto.yml`. The API reference sidebar and the changelog, CLI, Go, Rust, MCP, user guide, section, custom page, tag and page status steps now record their navbar links, sidebars, resources, render exclusions and script data in build state. The `Copy assets` step applies them in step order before merging the site settings, which removes about ten reads and writes of the file per build.

Two placement rules are now shared by every step. A contributed sidebar replaces all sidebars with the same id and goes last, and script data precedes the first after-body include that loads its script, by file name or as an embedded script. Builds are unchanged: the only steps that contribute sidebars already replaced one that was last.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: read and write each version's configuration once in versioned builds
description:
This makes a versioned build read each version's Quarto configuration once, apply every change in memory and write it once. Before, each change to navigation, page descriptions, the title, the site address or upcoming badges read and rewrote the file, and navigation pruning silently ignored errors reading or writing it. An unreadable configuration now stops the build, as it already did when setting the title. The generated sites are unchanged.

The layer also stops a historical version from hiding unexpected failures while it prunes CLI pages for commands its release lacks. Unreadable or incomplete caches and pages that cannot be changed are still skipped, but other errors, such as a JSON list where a mapping is expected, now stop the build instead of being ignored.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: test: wait for the edit to reach the preview in the Quarto project diff's watch case
description:
This makes the Quarto project diff's watch case record the same run every time, so maintainers can trust a comparison of a commit with itself. The case edits a user guide page, waits for watch mode to rebuild, then interrupts it. It decided that the rebuild had happened by finding the edit anywhere in the package, including the staging directory watch mode prepares inside the cache. The interrupt therefore often arrived before the preview had received the edit, and recorded runs differed in build steps, handled exceptions and previewed files from one run to the next.

The stub `quarto preview` now records the directory it serves, and the case waits for the edit to appear there. Every recorded watch run holds the full rebuild before the interrupt. The harness runs from the checkout under test on both sides of a comparison, so existing builds are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: configure parallel renders from the build's site configuration
description:
This makes parallel renders use the configuration the build assembled, to decide whether to split the site and to write each worker's reduced configuration, instead of reading `_quarto.yml` again. A user pre-render script's edits to `_quarto.yml` now reach the workers through one re-read after such scripts, from which the workers' configurations are written. Great Docs' own freeze-restore script leaves the file alone, so a build without user scripts reads nothing.

The layer also rewords three docstrings about the wide layout, appearance and GitHub navbar settings, which referred to a second configuration pass that no longer exists. Builds are otherwise unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: compare watch mode's project settings in memory
description:
This removes the last reads of `_quarto.yml` outside the build's own steps that no longer had a reason to exist. After each rebuild, `great-docs build --watch` read the previewed and staged files to decide whether to print its restart notice. It now compares the `project` settings of the last two preparations in memory. The notice keeps its wording and position, and a failed rebuild still leaves the preview at the last good build.

Reading or editing a build directory's `_quarto.yml` now requires the file and no longer adds website defaults, an option only tests used; the test helpers supply those defaults. `great-docs changelog` still edits the existing file to add its navbar link. Build behaviour is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: assemble the site configuration once during "Copy assets"
description:
This makes a build assemble Great Docs' site settings into `_quarto.yml` once. Preparation merged them, then "Copy assets" merged them again with the recorded build contributions, though the steps between the two passes no longer needed the first result. Preparation now writes only the initial configuration and the API reference block, and "Copy assets" assembles the rest and fetches the GitHub star, fork and release data.

Three outputs change. `_quarto.yml` places `jupyter` directly after `format` instead of near the end of its top-level keys, `project.resources` lists `assets/**` before the resources that build steps contribute, such as `_shared/**` and `objects.inv`, and settings that copy files into the build directory, such as the favicon conversion, run once per build instead of twice. `api-reference` stays the last top-level key. Include lists, filters and values are unchanged. A header include file that is missing now stops the build at "Copy assets" instead of "Prepare build directory".

The layer also records the Reference navbar link and sidebar together, and applies contributions after the navbar and script includes exist. Both leave builds unchanged.

title: refactor: pass the Quarto configuration to freeze-cache and sidebar sharing
description:
This makes two preparation steps work on a Quarto configuration passed to them instead of each reading `_quarto.yml` through its own wrapper. Freeze-cache preparation hands the configuration to the page metadata writer, and sidebar sharing trims the caller's configuration in place. Versioned builds already held each version's configuration and now pass it to sidebar sharing before writing it once.

The build step reads the file and writes it back only when sidebars are shared. Rendered output is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: write the site configuration once when preparation ends
description:
This makes preparation hold the Quarto configuration in memory and write `_quarto.yml` once, instead of reading and rewriting it in each step that touched it. The API reference, site settings, page metadata, terminal recordings and shared sidebars all work on the mapping, and a final unlisted step saves it. A single-version build writes the file twice, the initial skeleton that marks the directory as generated and the finished configuration, and preparation never reads it.

When dynamic introspection fails, the static-analysis retry changes only the in-memory configuration and the final write saves it. The internal API reference builder takes a mapping only, as every build already passed one. Builds, watch rebuilds and freezes are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: use the API reference recorded by the build instead of reading it back
description:
This removes the reads of `_quarto.yml` that the API reference step, the sidebar and the generated site content made to find a block the build had just written. `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `SKILL.md` and the homepage's llms links now use the recorded API reference configuration, and the skill's site URL comes from `site_url` in `great-docs.yml`, the only source of `website.site-url`. A Documentation URL in `pyproject.toml` still takes precedence.

Preparation always writes a fresh configuration and discovers exports, so the API reference step no longer checks for an existing block, repeats discovery or has a refresh path, and the site URL warning drops a fallback read that never supplied a URL. Builds, their output and their messages are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: let build contributions carry script data and navbar placements
description:
This lets build steps hand their navigation and script changes to the configuration step instead of editing `_quarto.yml` themselves. A contribution could only add a limited set of items, so the section, custom page, user guide, tag and page status steps each read and rewrote the file to place their links, sidebars and script data.

Contributions can now hold script data placed before the script that reads it, section and custom-page links placed after a matching English or translated label, the User Guide link placed before Reference, and untitled sidebars. Matching translated labels needs the site's language, so applying a contribution now always takes the project's configuration. No step uses the new placements yet, so generated output is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: resolve the site's name from configuration once per build
description:
This stops builds from re-reading the generated Quarto configuration to learn the site title. A build resolved the name and addresses at start-up, then up to eight later steps read the title back from `_quarto.yml`, including one read of the previous build's output. The title could depend on which file was on disk rather than on `great-docs.yml` and the project metadata.

The name now comes from the configured display name, then the package name, then the Go or Rust program when its CLI reference is enabled, matching the title already written to the configuration. Page titles, social cards, structured data, canonical links, sitemaps and crawler rules are unchanged. Versioned builds still add a version suffix only to each older version's copy.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: rebuild the previewed site on source edits in `great-docs build --watch`
description:
Authors running `great-docs build --watch` now see their edits in the preview. Watch mode ran `quarto preview` on the project prepared at start-up, so later edits to pages, assets and `great-docs.yml` never reached it.

It now watches the directory holding `great-docs.yml`, ignoring hidden and generated directories. After each batch of edits it reloads the configuration, prepares the project in a staging directory inside the cache, copies changed files into the previewed project and removes files that preparation no longer generates, leaving Quarto's rendered output alone. Configuration edits are picked up while the preview keeps running, and a change to the generated `project` settings prints a notice asking for a restart. A failed rebuild, including one from invalid configuration, leaves the preview at the last good build and watching continues.

This adds `watchfiles` as a dependency for file system events. The building guide now explains watch mode and says that `great-docs preview` does not rebuild after source edits.

title: refactor: render and finish builds through step modules
description:
This moves the build's rendering and finishing code out of the `GreatDocs` object so maintainers can read and test each step alone. Rendering a single-version or versioned site, copying to a separate site directory, writing the SEO files and timings, saving the freeze cache and the API snapshot all sat on the same large object.

Each step is now a module function with explicit inputs that returns its outcome. Values that depend on the site title, which earlier steps can change, are read when the step runs. Builds, their log and their output are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: link each project's API reference to its own source
description:
Building the API references of two projects in one process now links each to its own repository, ref and root. The renderer cached the source-link values the first time it read them, so the second project linked to the first project's source. Constructing a documentation project also wrote those values to the process environment and ran `git`, which is why they leaked between projects.

The API reference step now resolves the source links once per build and passes them to the renderer, and runs `git` only when links point to a GitHub repository. The snapshot's tag lookup retries once and times out after 5 seconds like the ref lookup, so one start failure no longer names a versioned build's snapshot `dev`. A `git` failure now warns under the API reference step in the build log.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: run build preparation and site configuration through step modules
description:
This moves the first build step next to the other build steps, so maintainers find preparation in the same place as rendering and publishing. It replaces the build directory, writes the initial Quarto project and configures the site, API reference, homepage and project pages. The steps share one resolution of site identity, default search descriptions and structured data, which the `seo` command now uses too.

The fallback homepage for `homepage: user_guide` with no guide pages is written by the user guide step, and the assets step merges site settings into the Quarto configuration, so neither needs a callback from the build coordinator. The homepage writer always rewrites `index.qmd`, as builds already did; the path that kept an existing homepage was used only by tests and is gone.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: skip the API reference without prompting when no package is detected
description:
Builds that cannot detect a package now warn and continue without an API reference, and no longer ask for a package name on standard input. Captured build output hid the prompt until the read finished, and an MCP build could consume a line of the protocol stream. Skipping gives the result of leaving the old prompt unanswered.

Build steps also share one set of project facts read at the start of each build: the package name, packaging metadata and GitHub repository. Each use used to reread the name, and metadata was cached per `GreatDocs` instance, so edits to packaging files between builds never reached a long-running MCP server. They do now.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: feat: let `package_info_page` switch off PyPI release-date requests
description:
Site authors can now keep the package-info page without it querying PyPI. The page asked PyPI for the latest release date of every dependency on each build, and `package_info_page` could only turn the whole page on or off.

The option now also takes a mapping. With `release_dates: false` the build makes no PyPI request and the dependency tables drop the "Last Published" column. `true`, `false` and a mapping that omits a field behave as before, a bare `package_info_page:` still disables the page, and any other value stops the build with a configuration error. GitHub requests are unchanged.

```yaml
package_info_page:
  enabled: true        # Generate the page
  release_dates: true  # Query PyPI once per dependency on each build for its latest release date
```

The `great-docs.yml` that `great-docs init` writes now shows this mapping as a comment, so the Quarto project diff reports the `init` scaffold for 5 packages. Built sites are unchanged.

title: fix: read a Poetry 1.x project's name, module and URLs in the build
description:
Poetry 1.x projects now build with their name, description, authors, repository and package location. The build read only `[project]` in `pyproject.toml`, so a `[tool.poetry]` project had no package name, an empty description and no GitHub repository, and `great-docs init` listed no authors. Module detection also ignored Poetry's `packages`, and the search for `__init__.py` treated setuptools `packages.find` as a list of packages and never looked in its `where` directories.

The build, `init` and module detection now read the shared project metadata reader. `setup.cfg` fills each field that `pyproject.toml` leaves empty, and `init` lists its authors and maintainers. Project URL labels match whatever their case and separators, so `Source Code` or `REPOSITORY` now gives a repository and its star widget, source links and changelog. The package name comes only from a `name` keyword in `setup.py`.

The package metadata no longer carries a copy of 26 configuration settings. The CLI reference, the homepage developer cards and the citation page read the configuration directly. Finding the package directory no longer raises and catches a `ValueError` per layout directory, which is the only difference the Quarto project diff reports.

title: refactor: generate reference pages and site files through build step modules
description:
This moves reference-page and site-file generation into build step modules so maintainers can read and test them one at a time. The API, interlinks, Click, Go and Rust CLI, and MCP reference steps, the generated site files, and the passes for freeze caches, mock-code cells, d2 diagrams, terminal recordings and shared sidebars all lived on the `GreatDocs` object.

Step order, titles, warnings and failure handling are unchanged. Freeze cache preparation reads the site description and structured data when the step runs, as custom page publishing does.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: stop a malformed `authors` entry from blocking the changelog, proofread, seo and MCP tools
description:
The `changelog`, `proofread` and `seo` commands and the MCP status tool and `gd://reference/` resource no longer fail on an `authors` entry that is not a mapping, such as a bare name. They built a whole `GreatDocs` instance first, which resolved author portraits and the site name at start-up, though they need only the configuration and packaging files.

They now read those files directly and report the same layout and configuration errors and the same command output. Directories for a clean build are validated against freshly read configuration, and the build itself still runs through the documentation project.
