title: refactor: write the initial `great-docs.yml` from the install module
description:
This changes only the code behind `great-docs init`, so maintainers can read it in one place. The initial `great-docs.yml` was written by a `GreatDocs` method that also detected the docstring style, dynamic mode, module, authors and reference sections.

The writer now lives beside the `.gitignore` update and receives the configuration, layout, project facts and export discovery from `GreatDocs.install()`. The text it prints and writes is unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: report a missing package in the MCP reference resource and completions
description:
MCP clients now get a clear answer for a project whose package cannot be detected. The `gd://reference/{symbol}` resource answered with an internal error about `NoneType`, and symbol completions for `improve-docstrings` and the reference template failed silently. The resource now says the package name could not be detected, as the scan and API-surface handlers do, and both completions offer an empty list.

The project facts that builds and commands read now include the module to document, the import name, the package's `__init__.py`, the candidate package directories and whether the package is a compiled extension. Builds, the CLI, the MCP server and the linter read these instead of detecting them again at each use, and the search for `__init__.py` skips a file named `src`, `python` or `lib` where it expected a directory.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: read Poetry 1.x metadata and `setup.cfg` names in every command
description:
Projects that declare their metadata in `[tool.poetry]`, `setup.cfg` or `setup.py` are now found by every command. `skill install`, `skill list`, `api-diff`, `api-snapshot`, `check-examples`, versioned API pages and the layout migration read the package name only from `[project]` in `pyproject.toml`, so such projects had no package name outside the build.

One project metadata reader now serves these commands, the CLI reference and the extras installed by remote builds and `setup-github-pages`. It reads the first file that declares each value and names the file when one cannot be parsed, so a malformed `setup.cfg` beside a valid `pyproject.toml` now counts as unreadable metadata. The layout migration also protects packages listed by a hatch wheel target and a dotted setuptools package at its own path, and a `username = "bob"` line before `setup(name="realpkg")` no longer names the package `bob`.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: run documentation builds through a build pipeline
description:
This moves the build's coordination out of `GreatDocs.build` into a build pipeline module, so the freeze command and the Gauntlet site builder reuse the same preparation steps. `GreatDocs.build` keeps its signature and delegates preparation, rendering, finishing and watch mode, and the freeze command no longer constructs a `GreatDocs` instance. Page authors are read when each build starts instead of at construction, with the same values.

The build header's version, package directory and page-count lookups now catch specific exceptions instead of every exception. A missing distribution leaves the version blank and a missing `git` executable leaves the package directory in the header, as before, but an unexpected error now stops the build. The Quarto project diff reports only that the header's `PackageNotFoundError` and watch's `KeyboardInterrupt` are now raised from the pipeline module; no generated file differs.

title: refactor: publish content through build step functions
description:
This turns the build's content publishing into module functions so maintainers can test them without a `GreatDocs` object. The user guide, section, custom page and asset steps were methods on that object, which made their inputs implicit.

Published pages, sidebars, navbar links, Quarto resources and printed messages are unchanged. Raw custom pages take the site's identity, structured data and default description when the step runs, since earlier steps can change the site title.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: reload packages and exports on every build
description:
A second `build()` on the same `GreatDocs` object, or `build()` after `install()`, now sees changes to package source and exclusion settings. It reused the package model and exports from the earlier call, so removing an export made the next build fail because the reference still listed it.

Package loading, export discovery and reference section generation now share one object built from the configuration and project facts, which each build and initialisation create afresh. The `scan` command, `api-diff --graph`, `api-snapshot`, lint and the MCP scan tool, API surface resource and symbol completions read the configuration and packaging files directly instead of setting up a documentation project. A malformed `authors` entry, such as a bare name, therefore no longer stops them, and quiet lint restores standard output on every exit.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: quote author names that `great-docs init` writes when YAML requires it
description:
Site authors whose names, roles or emails contain YAML syntax now get a valid `great-docs.yml` from `great-docs init`. The `authors:` block copied values from `pyproject.toml` unquoted, so a name such as `Doe, Jane: PhD` or `@jane` made the file invalid and builds fell back to the default settings. `Jane #1` was read as `Jane`, and `true` or `123` became a boolean or a number.

Values are now quoted only when YAML needs it, and multi-line values use block scalars. Plain names such as `Jane Doe` produce the same output as before. The block is formatted by the project set-up module instead of a `GreatDocs` method.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: feat: Write a WebMCP manifest for each rendered version
description:
This PR adds a new build step that writes `gd-webmcp.json` to the root of each rendered version when `webmcp` is enabled. It is the static index the site's WebMCP tools will read. The listed pages come from the version's rendered `search.json`, ordered by section and then by sidebar position, and each page carries its title, kind (page, guide, post, api, cli, mcp, reference), sidebar group, description, tags, status, date and the `.md` copy when one exists. 

The manifest also lists the API objects from `objects.inv` with their short-name aliases (names claimed by two objects are dropped), the CLI commands, the changelog's release headings, and which agent files exist (llms.txt, skills, MCP manifest, search index). Each manifest's paths are relative to its own version root, so a versioned site gets one manifest per version, each describing its own API, version and URL.

The facts file written before rendering now records section ids and kinds plus page tags, status and date, and a page can stay out of the manifest with `webmcp: {listed: false}` while keeping its tools. Output is compact JSON with sorted keys, so repeat builds produce identical files, and a missing or unreadable input produces a build warning rather than a failure.

title: feat: WebMCP runtime core with get_current_page and per-page opt-out
description:
This PR adds the browser runtime for WebMCP, `great_docs/assets/webmcp.js`. When `webmcp.enabled` is on, every page loads it in the head, deferred, after a JSON settings block and any `origin_trials` `<meta>` tags. The runtime validates tool input against each tool's schema and returns errors as data with the schema and an example, because the browser doesn't validate input and drops thrown error messages.

It registers tools through `document.modelContext` (falling back to `navigator.modelContext`) under one shared abort signal, records the outcome in `data-gd-webmcp` on `<html>`, and, when `js_api` is on, exposes `window.greatDocs.tools` with `list`, `call` and `add` plus a `gd-webmcp:ready` event. The first tool, `get_current_page`, returns the page's Markdown from its `.md` copy, falling back to the rendered page when that copy can't be fetched, and offers an outline format and a `max_chars` limit that truncates on a line break and closes any open code fence. A new build step, "Prepare WebMCP pages", adds a `gd-no-webmcp` body class to pages with `webmcp: false` in their front matter, which tells the runtime to register no tools there. The step also writes `_gd_webmcp_pages.json` with each page's title, description, section and draft status for later tools. The runtime is tested in Node against a stub page and a stub `modelContext`, covering registration, refusals, input validation, Markdown handling and the size limit. With WebMCP off by default, the only change to existing builds is the new skipped step, which renumbers the build log.

title: test: cover the term player's forked child and other leaf-module paths
description:
Coverage now includes the term player's forked child process, tested with fork and exec stubbed, the `0.0.0` version of an uninstalled package, a namespace package without skills, and a recording that starts before time zero.

Three kinds of unreachable code are deleted: the import fallbacks for the `importlib_metadata` backport and older griffe releases, which the supported Python and griffe versions never take; the progress bar's handler for a closed pipe, which the stream writer already swallows; and a second error handler around parsing a term-player script that validation has already cleaned. Nothing changes for users.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: test: cover the API renderer's extension point and empty sections
description:
Coverage now includes the API renderer's extension point, exercised by a renderer subclass defined outside Great Docs, and its handling of empty Parameters and Returns sections. The base render methods, which hold only docstrings, count as covered on import. The type-only import in the pandoc components uses `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, which coverage already excludes.

Two width checks in the conversion of RST tables are deleted: the patterns that recognise a table guarantee enough columns, so neither check could fail. Tables convert as before.

title: test: cover marimo islands and colour parsing, and drop unreachable table and d2 branches
description:
Coverage now includes the marimo island generators and the rejection of five- and seven-digit hex colours, which tests now exercise.

Five branches that no input reaches are deleted: the CSV fallback after every known table file format, a column type check that an earlier check already answers, an error handler around a float NaN test, a pass-through for notebook lines the cell pattern never captures, and a handler for d2 pages outside the d2 directory. Files with an unknown extension still preview as CSV, and builds are unchanged.

title: test: cover the versioned build's copying and reference pruning
description:
Coverage of versioned builds now includes copying a historical version, skipping its internal files and pruning its API reference, which builds run but coverage excluded. Tests now cover them, including replacing an existing version directory and keeping subdirectories and non-page files during pruning.

The version badge's fallback for a type other than `new`, `changed` or `deprecated` is deleted: the marker accepts only those three, so no input reached it. Badges render as before.

title: test: cover the MCP server's request handlers
description:
Coverage now includes the MCP server's request handling: the adapters that receive each kind of client request, and the server's stdio entry point, were excluded from it. Tests send every request kind through an in-process client and run the server over in-memory streams. A fallback for a server without an `instructions` attribute, dead since mcp 2.0 became the minimum, is deleted; the instructions now go to the server's constructor and clients receive the same text.

The tests turned up a bug, fixed in its own commit: completions ignored the `project_path` and `config_path` the request's context selects, and completed from the working directory. With the server started in a project's parent directory, completing a `gd://page/{path}` offered `project/user_guide/intro.qmd` instead of `user_guide/intro.qmd`. Completions now use the selected project, as tools and resources already did.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: report only project problems as failed MCP tool calls
description:
The MCP server now answers an unexpected error with a protocol error, and keeps serving. Its tools, the API surface and symbol reference resources, and the symbol completions caught every exception, so a bug in Great Docs reached the client as a failed tool call or error text, as if the project were at fault, and completions came back empty without saying why. The project's own problems are reported as before: an invalid configuration or layout, file errors, a package that fails to import or load, and a failed build.

A tool call that omits a required argument, such as `gd_add_page` without `title`, now gets `Error: missing required argument: title` before the tool runs, where it got `Error: 'title'`. The server does not check argument types against the tool schemas, so a wrongly typed argument now gives a protocol error.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: require mcp 2.0 and stop MCP introspection hiding unexpected errors
description:
The `mcp` extra now requires `mcp>=2.0.0`, and the MCP reference pages and the Great Docs MCP server drop their mcp 1.x code, so environments pinned to mcp 1.x must upgrade. Under mcp 2.0, `python -m great_docs.mcp` crashed at start-up with a `TypeError`; it now starts and answers clients.

When the MCP reference pages introspect a server, any error used to send them to a scan of the server's source, and listing resources, templates and prompts treated any failure as an empty list. A bug therefore left pages with missing sections and no explanation. The source scan now follows only a missing `mcp` package, a server that cannot start or be reached, a timeout or a protocol error, also when these arrive grouped, and its notice names the underlying error. Listing treats only protocol errors and timeouts as empty.

Errors outside these types now raise instead of being swallowed. A build reports such an error as the step's warning when it is a user-code error type, such as `AttributeError`, and stops on anything else, including a group that mixes expected and unexpected errors.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: keep the API discovery cache when a project moves
description:
The API discovery cache that `great-docs build --no-refresh` reads now survives moving or re-cloning a project. Its key included the absolute path of every package file, so a project in a new directory discovered its API reference again instead of reusing the saved sections.

For maintainers, the Quarto project diff no longer reports a difference in every case under `--fail-on difference`, even for `main` against itself. The diff builds the base and the head in different directories, and the cache key also changes with the great-docs version, so the cache file differed every time. The diff now ignores the key and compares the cached sections.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: feat: add `webmcp` configuration option
description:
This PR adds the `webmcp` option to `great-docs.yml`, the first step toward registering WebMCP tools that in-browser AI agents can call. The option is off by default. It accepts `true`/`false` shorthand or a mapping with `enabled`, `actions`, `js_api`, `exclude_tools` and `origin_trials`, declared in `great-docs.default.yml` and exposed through new `Config.webmcp_*` properties

The two lists are checked when the config loads: malformed values raise a `ConfigError`, while an unknown name in `exclude_tools` only prints a warning listing the known tools, so renaming a tool later won't break existing builds. A new `webmcp_tools` module lists all 17 built-in tools with their titles, purposes and the site feature each one needs, and config checking uses it.

title: fix: compare the Quarto project diff with the branch point by default
description:
When run locally without `--base`, `make quarto-project-diff` now compares the checkout with the commit where `HEAD` branched from `main`, not with the tip of `main`.

Once `main` moved past a branch's starting point, the report also included the output changes from every commit that had landed on `main` since then. They appeared reversed, as if the branch had made them, so a refactor run with `--fail-on difference` could fail for changes it never touched. On an up-to-date branch the two bases are the same commit. CI passes `--base` explicitly and is unaffected.

title: Add WebMCP platform probe for Chrome
description:
This PR adds `scripts/webmcp_probe/`, a small probe that checks how Chrome actually implements WebMCP, so the upcoming `webmcp.js` runtime is built on observed behavior rather than the draft spec. A test page registers about twenty tools covering return types, annotations, name rules, cancellation signals, iframes and navigation. A dependency-free Node runner (`run.mjs`) launches Chrome with a throwaway profile and calls those tools through the DevTools protocol's `WebMCP` domain, which is the same path agent extensions use.

A run against Chrome 157, it showed that the API lives only on `document.modelContext` and that `registerTool` returns a promise that rejects on errors. It also showed that tool input is not checked against the schema, results pass through unwrapped, and a thrown error reaches the agent with no message. Navigating right after returning a result still delivers that result. A README explains how to run the probe and lists the few checks that need a person with the Model Context Tool Inspector.

title: test: trim the Quarto project diff to its comparison and regression checks
description:
The Quarto project diff no longer counts handled exceptions or lists known gaps. It keeps the comparison of two commits, the 40-case tier that CI runs, the full catalogue behind `make quarto-project-diff-full`, the regression verdict and the fail-on-difference marker. The exception census served the core refactor's exception policy; with the refactor done, a newly handled exception is a matter for code review, and the refactor's pull requests show no regression that the census or the gaps caught and the tests missed. With the census go the observer loaded into every great-docs process, the Python process counts and the Python 3.12 floor. Recordings made before this change are refused.

The two known gaps, watch mode not rebuilding after a source edit and freeze preparing different files after a build, are fixed, so each is now a failed check and a recurrence fails the run.

Once this merges, #604 and the pull request that stops API snapshots hiding unexpected errors differ from `main` only in what the census reported, so they can carry the fail-on-difference marker.

title: ci: test the lowest and highest dependency versions
description:
CI now runs the tests twice instead of four times: on Python 3.11 with the lowest allowed version of each direct dependency, and on Python 3.14 with the newest version of everything. Both install with uv. Adding a job per Python release grows the matrix with every release, so CI now tests only the two ends of the supported range and no longer runs on 3.12 or 3.13.

Testing the lowest versions showed that several minimums in `pyproject.toml` did not work. Users now need click 8.2, requests 2.27 and Pillow 9.2. The `mcp`, `docs` and `dev` extras need mcp 1.21.1, pandas 2.2.2, pyarrow 16.0, pytest 7.3 and typer 0.16. Older mcp releases fail to import with current pydantic, and older pandas and pyarrow releases fail to import with NumPy 2.

title: ci: authenticate the d2 installer's GitHub API request
description:
The d2 install step in the test, checks and docs workflows now passes the workflow token to the installer.

The installer looks up the release checksum through the GitHub API. Without a token, that request counts against the anonymous limit of 60 requests an hour, which every job on the same runner IP shares. Once the limit is spent, the step fails with a 403 and the job needs a rerun. With the token, the request counts against the repository's own, much higher limit.

title: test: cover explicit API reference sections
description:
Coverage now includes the API reference code for explicit sections without contents, unnamed items and module entries holding a class large enough to have its methods listed separately, and the generated reference configuration's blank lines between class groups and method counts on small classes. Configuration reaches all of it, but coverage excluded it; tests now cover each case. Nothing changes for users.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: test: cover user guide and custom page edge cases
description:
Coverage now includes the user guide and custom page code for unusual input, which configuration reaches but coverage excluded: unreadable guide pages, listed items that are neither a name nor a mapping, pages outside the guide directory, empty sections and unnamed items in an explicit sidebar, pages named only by their ordering prefix, navbar values without a label, and custom pages with an unsupported layout. Tests now cover each case. Nothing changes for users.

title: test: cover the CLI reference pages
description:
Coverage of the CLI reference pages now includes sidebar ordering by `cli.sections`, index sections that name a missing or hidden command, and help text with bullet lists, which tests now exercise.

Two unreachable branches are deleted rather than tested: the index's skip of hidden subcommands, which every extractor already drops, and a Rust summary branch that ran only when a description's first sentence was longer than the whole description. Generated pages are unchanged.

title: fix: let unexpected errors surface in skill checks, PR previews and the term-player editor
description:
Three tools off the build path now let an error they do not expect show its traceback instead of treating it as an ordinary failure. `great-docs termshow edit` still answers a malformed request or an unwritable script with 400 and a preview Quarto cannot render with 500. A bug in the editor now prints its traceback in the editor's terminal and drops the connection, where the browser was told its request was bad.

The `great-docs skill` commands fall back as before for a package that is not installed or a version they cannot parse, and `great-docs preview --pr` still ignores a `.env` file it cannot read or decode when looking for a token. Any other error in either now propagates.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: report only expected errors from the evolution, icon and colour swatch shortcodes
description:
The evolution, icon and colour swatch shortcodes now show the traceback of an error Great Docs does not expect. The page still renders with an HTML comment in place of the shortcode, but the comment holds the traceback instead of one line, so a bug in Great Docs no longer reads like a problem with the page. Expected failures keep their one-line comment: a release whose package or `pyproject.toml` fails to load, git and file errors, an unknown palette or invalid colour, and Great Docs' source not being found from Quarto's Python.

The colour swatch also handles two kinds of bad entry better. An item in its list that is not a mapping, such as a bare number, is now skipped like other incomplete items instead of stopping the swatch. An unquoted hex (`hex: #ff0000`, which YAML reads as empty) or a numeric name still stops it, but the comment now shows the entry and says to quote the hex value.

title: fix: show the traceback when a CLI command fails unexpectedly
description:
CLI commands now show the traceback of an error that Great Docs does not expect, instead of a one-line `Error: <message>`. Every command caught every exception, so a bug in Great Docs looked like a problem with the user's project and left nothing to debug from. The exit status stays 1.

Problems in the project or its environment are reported as before: an invalid configuration or layout, a file that cannot be read or written, a file that is not UTF-8 and, for commands that load the package, a package that fails to import. With `--json`, `seo`, `lint` and `api-diff` keep their JSON error object for those problems but print the traceback for an unexpected error. `freeze --info` and `api-snapshot` still mark a page or tag they cannot read and carry on. Interrupting the overwrite question of `config` or `setup-github-pages` now prints `Aborted!` instead of an empty `Error:` line.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: warn when check-examples cannot read docstring examples
description:
`great-docs check-examples` now warns when it cannot collect a package's docstring examples. A package that failed to load, or a documented object reached through an import that does not resolve, was skipped without a word, so its examples went unchecked. The warnings print above the summary and appear as a `warnings` list in the `--json` output; the exit code is unchanged. A documented object that is itself a broken import no longer stops the command with a traceback.

A page is now reported as an error only for the failures a render can expect: Quarto failing to start, output that does not decode, file errors and a broken worker pool. Any other exception is a bug in Great Docs and shows its traceback instead of passing as a page error.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: stop `great-docs lint` skipping class members on unexpected errors
description:
`great-docs lint` no longer skips a class's members when it meets an error it does not expect. The docstring checks wrapped each class and each docstring read in handlers that caught any error, so a run could pass while checking less than it said. Only an export or member that is an alias griffe cannot resolve, because its target is missing or part of an import cycle, is still skipped, and the rest of the package is linted as before. Errors outside these types now raise instead of being swallowed.

The stale-version check now uses the configuration the command has already loaded instead of reading `great-docs.yml` again. A `great-docs.yml` holding a list or a single value used to crash the check; the loader warns about such a file and uses the defaults, so the check reports nothing.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: stop API snapshots hiding unexpected errors
description:
API snapshots, which feed `great-docs api-diff`, the MCP `gd_api_diff` tool and the version badges of versioned builds, now raise on an error they do not expect instead of silently losing data. Reading a symbol's parameters, base classes, decorators and annotations, and the package's exports, each sat in a handler that caught any error and recorded an empty value or left the symbol out, so a bug could thin or empty a snapshot without a word.

The one expected failure, an export whose alias target is missing or cyclic, is handled as before: an unresolvable `__all__` falls back to the public members, and an unresolvable export is left out. Any other error now raises instead of being swallowed. Snapshots record the same values as before.

title: refactor: drop the repeat-call guarantees of site settings
description:
Site settings no longer search the Quarto configuration for entries from an earlier call to replace or remove them. A build assembles `_quarto.yml` once and calls each setting once, yet the wide layout, appearance, navigation label, release badge, reference switcher and version selector settings kept code for a second call, with docstrings and tests promising that it would leave the configuration unchanged. That code, those promises and their tests are gone.

Two kinds of check stay. Contributions still skip navbar links, resources and render exclusions that are already present, because `great-docs changelog` applies its contribution to a built site that may already link the changelog. The theme, signature grammar, header includes and Font Awesome are still added only when missing, because the user's `site:` settings may already list them. Builds are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: test: report the page result when a real Quarto example check fails
description:
The `check-examples` tests that render a page with real Quarto now print the whole page result, including its error message, when a status assertion fails. These tests occasionally fail in a loaded parallel suite, and the failure showed only the unexpected status, or only that `check.log` was missing. Nothing said whether Quarto timed out, exited with an error or produced no output.

This does not fix the flake, which did not reproduce under deliberate load. The log-file test now asserts that its page failed before it reads the log, so it too reports the status. The next failure should name its cause.

title: test: name the reference-section tests after the function they call
description:
The tests that build API reference sections from the `reference` configuration are renamed after the function they exercise. Their names and docstrings still named a `GreatDocs` method that an earlier refactor removed, and each test created a `GreatDocs` object and a temporary directory it never used.

The tests now describe the configuration case each one checks, without the unused setup. Their assertions are unchanged.

title: refactor: read a project's configuration from its layout in one place
description:
The build, the CLI commands, the MCP server, the pull request preview, export discovery and the examples checker now load `great-docs.yml` through the resolved project layout. Each used to build the configuration by hand from the layout's package root, configuration file and cache directory, and a copy that forgot the file or the cache directory would read the root-level configuration or cache instead of the selected one.

The watch rebuild reloads the configuration the same way. `Config` keeps its public signature, and builds are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: build --from-repo with the running great-docs version
description:
`great-docs build --from-repo` now builds with the great-docs version that runs it. Its temporary environment installed the latest release from PyPI, which can differ from the running version. Release 0.17.0, for example, rejects the `--config` option the parent passes and writes the site where the parent does not look for it.

The environment now installs the running source tree when great-docs runs from a development checkout, and otherwise the same release, `great-docs==<version>`, from PyPI. If that install fails, the build stops with an error naming the requirement instead of installing another version. A development build installed from a wheel or a Git URL therefore cannot use `--from-repo`.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: keep both themes of a light and dark site theme
description:
Sites with a light and a dark theme now build with both. A `site.theme` mapping such as `{light: flatly, dark: darkly}` became `theme: [light, dark, great-docs.scss]` in the generated `_quarto.yml`, so the site got one Bootstrap stylesheet instead of the chosen themes, and no dark stylesheet.

Each mode now keeps its own list, with `great-docs.scss` placed as for a single theme: after the built-in themes and before the user's stylesheets. A mode given as one name becomes a list, so the example above becomes `light: [flatly, great-docs.scss]` and `dark: [darkly, great-docs.scss]`.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: make --no-refresh reuse the last build's API discovery
description:
`great-docs build --no-refresh` now skips API discovery when nothing it depends on has changed. The flag, and `GreatDocs.build(refresh=False)`, promised faster rebuilds but only changed a log line: every build discovered the package's exports again.

Every build now saves the API reference sections it discovers in the cache directory: `docs/.cache/` in a `docs/` layout, `.great-docs-cache/` when `great-docs.yml` sits at the project root. Both are already in the `.gitignore` that `great-docs init` writes. With `--no-refresh`, a build reuses the saved sections while the Great Docs version, `great-docs.yml` and the package's files are unchanged, and discovers again otherwise. Changes to dependencies or the Python version do not count. A build without the flag always discovers and updates the cache. The "Configure API reference" step now reads "Reused cached API discovery" or "API reference discovered".

title: fix: rebuild the API reference when package source changes during watch
description:
`great-docs build --watch` now rebuilds when you edit the documented package, and the preview shows the edit. Watch mode watched only the directory holding `great-docs.yml`. In a `docs/` layout the package sits outside it, so a docstring edit or a new export left the API reference stale until the watch restarted. Even when a rebuild ran, it reused the modules it had already imported, so dynamic introspection (the default) still read the old docstrings.

Watch mode now also watches the package's directory, with the same exclusions, for every project whose package it finds. That includes projects with `reference: false`, because the CLI and MCP pages also read the package. Each rebuild imports the package's own modules afresh. A change to `module:` while watching takes effect after a restart. The `--watch` help and the Watch Mode guide now say package edits are watched.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: count only the steps watch mode runs in its build log
description: The log of `great-docs build --watch` now announces only the steps watch mode runs. Its header counted the finishing steps that follow a full render, which watch mode skips because it serves a live preview, so it announced 20 steps and its footer reported 19 of 20 complete. Both now say 19. Full builds are unchanged.

title: fix: give the right hint when freeze cannot find a page
description:
`great-docs freeze PAGE` now gives a useful hint when the page is not in the prepared site. It suggested running `great-docs build` first, which never helped: freeze prepares the site itself before it looks for the page. The page is missing because the site does not publish it, and the hint now says so: "The site does not publish this page. Freeze renders only pages of the user guide, the configured sections and the custom pages."

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: make the MCP API-diff tool compare a git ref with the working tree
description:
The `gd_api_diff` MCP tool now works. It failed on every call: it relied on snapshot methods that do not exist and looked for saved snapshots that nothing writes. Its tests patched in the missing method, so they passed.

With `base`, the tool compares the API at that git ref with the working tree, or with `head` when given (before, `head` was only a label). Without `base`, it lists the current API. It reads the working tree from the project's source, so the package need not be installed, and lists added, removed and changed symbols with the details of each change. The `base` description, shown on the tool's reference page, no longer promises a default of the previous release tag.

Snapshots at a git tag now read the tag's source. Run from the root of a flat-layout project, `great-docs api-diff v0.2 HEAD` loaded the package in the current directory for both sides and reported no changes; it now reports them. The build's version badges use the same snapshots.

title: refactor: type the Go and Rust CLI command trees
description:
The Go and Rust CLI extractors now return the same typed command tree as the Click extractor, and strict pyright checks both. They returned untyped dictionaries and sat on pyright's exclude list, so the reference build cast each result and silenced pyright on their imports.

A command without examples now records an empty list instead of an empty string, as the shared tree declares. CLI pages are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: name the Typer apps Typer cannot convert when no command is found
description:
When CLI discovery finds no command and Typer could not convert an app it met, for example because a parameter has a type Typer does not support, the build now warns and names each such app with Typer's error. Before, the error was hidden and discovery reported only that it found no command, so the author had no hint why the site had no CLI pages. Discovery still skips an app it cannot convert and keeps looking, so a later command in the module is documented as before, and `llms-full.txt` is still written without the CLI.

This PR also narrows three other handlers on the build path. Colour in the build log is turned off only for a closed or missing standard output, the marimo islands version falls back to the pinned release only when marimo is not installed, and a directory's sidebar metadata reads as empty only when its file cannot be read or is not valid YAML. Errors outside these types now raise instead of being swallowed.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: find CLI commands in the modules that project scripts name
description:
Packages whose command lives only in the module a script names now get CLI reference pages. The CLI guide said discovery searched the entry point module from `[project.scripts]`, but discovery only tried the package's `cli`, `__main__`, `main`, `console` and `commands` modules. A package declaring `tool = "pkg.tools.entry:run"`, with its command in `pkg/tools/entry.py`, got no CLI pages.

With no `cli.module` set, discovery now tries those five modules first, then the module of each script in `[project.scripts]` and `[project.gui-scripts]`, in the order they are listed. In a module found this way, the object the script names is documented when it is a Click command or Typer app. A script module that fails to import gives a warning naming it, where discovery used to report no CLI. The CLI guide and the CLI recipe now list the full search order.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: show a Typer argument's help text on its CLI page
description:
CLI reference pages for Typer apps now show each argument's help text. An argument declared with `typer.Argument(help="Who to greet.")` read only `Required.` on its command's page; it now reads `Required. Who to greet.`. Click arguments take no help text, so Click pages are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: docs: list the pages that link checking and proofreading read
description:
The link checker and proofreading guides now list the pages the two checks read: the homepage source, the user guide, each section and custom page directory, and `README.md` at the package root. They also say what the checks skip: paths with a part starting with `_` or `.`, a `recipes/` directory that no section lists, and generated pages such as the API reference. The guides used to describe every `.qmd` and `.md` file in the docs directory.

They also correct three earlier statements. `{.gd-no-link}` works in `.md` pages as well as `.qmd` pages, and URLs on Python comment lines are not checked. `great-docs proofread recipes/` checks nothing, because a directory argument is not expanded into files, so the example now passes a glob.

title: fix: keep balanced parentheses in checked URLs
description:
The link checker now requests URLs with balanced parentheses whole. It cut every URL at its first closing parenthesis, so `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(language)` was requested without its final `)` and could be reported broken. A `{.gd-no-link}` marker after such a URL did not exclude it either.

A closing parenthesis with no matching opening one in the URL, as at the end of a Markdown link or a parenthesised aside, is still dropped along with trailing punctuation. As before, marking a URL once in a `.qmd` or `.md` file also excludes its unmarked repeats in that file.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: type the link check report
description:
`GreatDocs.check_links` now declares the shape of its report. It was annotated `-> dict`, so type checkers knew nothing of its keys or of the fields of redirect and broken-link entries, and strict pyright reported its callers and tests as partially unknown. The report is now a typed dictionary, `LinkReport`, with typed redirect and broken-link entries. The returned values and the JSON output are unchanged.

`GreatDocs(project_path=...)` now also accepts path objects in its annotation, as it already did at runtime.

The method's docstring and the link checker guide now say that `total` counts skipped URLs and that redirect and broken-link entries list the `files` containing each URL.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: share the checked-file lists between link checking and proofreading
description:
Link checking no longer depends on the proofreading module. It imported proofreading to find the documentation pages (the authored pages plus `README.md`) and the package's Python files, so one check relied on code that belongs to the other. Both lists now live in a module of their own that the two checks and the CLI share. Each check reads the same files as before.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: check a configured module's source files when the project has no distribution name
description:
`great-docs check-links` and `great-docs proofread --include-docstrings` now check the package's Python files whenever the module to document is known, whether or not the project has a distribution name. The `check_links` and `proofread` methods of `GreatDocs` behave the same way.

Before, these checks also required a distribution name. A project with no `pyproject.toml` or other packaging metadata and more than one package directory has none, so the checks ignored the `module` set in `great-docs.yml` and skipped every source file without saying so.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: page writers read their directories from the project layout
description:
The licence, citation and community pages, the homepage, page status and the skills writers now take the project layout instead of a package root and a build directory passed separately.

They took two paths because several tests assigned a new `GreatDocs.build_dir` after creating the project, which left the project's layout pointing at the old directory. Those tests now use the build directory their project resolves, so the writers can read it from the layout. Builds are unchanged.

`GreatDocs.project_root` and `GreatDocs.build_dir` stay for now. Removing them touches most test files, so it waits until the open pull requests have merged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: type the MCP request adapters with mcp's request models
description:
The MCP server's request adapters now take mcp 2's request parameter models and return its result models. Server behaviour is unchanged.

The adapters accepted `Any`, read fields with `getattr` and defaults left from supporting mcp 1 and 2, and found their handlers through an untyped lookup table. With `mcp>=2.0.0` required, none of that was needed, and it hid field access and handler calls from the type checker. The resource reader was also annotated as taking a URL while it always received a string.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor!: remove GreatDocs.project_root and GreatDocs.build_dir
description:
`GreatDocs` no longer has `project_root` and `build_dir` attributes. External code reads `docs.layout.package_root` and `docs.layout.build_dir`, and no alias remains.

Both attributes copied values the project's layout already holds, and the class docstring listed them as public. Nothing in the package needs them any more, since the writers take the layout.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: render each API reference with its own settings
description:
Render classes now read the settings of the reference they render from a required `settings` field. This is the supported way for a `Render*` subclass to read the language, signature style and source links. Constructing a renderer without it raises `TypeError`. Rendered output is unchanged.

The settings used to reach renderers through module state that `APIReference.build` set and restored, so renderers had no supported way to read them and the next render-affecting setting would have forced one. The state also made output depend on order: listing the documented objects of one reference could change how another rendered. Two references in one process now render with their own settings, in any order.

Object hooks still receive only the object, but version callouts translate their titles while objects are resolved. The reference language reaches them through one value scoped to the reference being resolved. The translation lookup the renderers call is renamed `translate`. This stacks on the `exclude_*` removal, which edits the same renderer mixins.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: share one definition of project errors between the CLI and MCP server
description:
The CLI and the MCP server now use one set of exceptions for problems in the project: invalid configuration or layout, file access failures and files that are not UTF-8. Every command and every MCP handler still reports exactly what it did before.

The two front ends each kept their own set, and they differed without a stated reason: the CLI's `COMMAND_ERRORS` and the server's `_PROJECT_ERRORS`, one underscore from a shared name. The MCP handlers still add package-loading errors and plain `ValueError` on top, and a comment now says why. This stacks on the argument validation change, which edits the same handlers.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: assume a fresh configuration when assembling site settings
description:
Site settings assembly no longer handles a navbar, footer or filter list that an earlier call left behind. Builds are unchanged.

A build assembles the settings once, on a configuration that holds only the project type and theme, and the user's `site:` settings merge into the HTML format. The code that replaced an existing GitHub entry, dropped a legacy Home link, skipped a footer attribution already present, or refused to prepare a shared sidebar twice could therefore never run. It also had tests of its own, which made the assembly harder to read.

This stacks on the layout change, because both edit the brand settings.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: write site pages and settings from the project's layout
description:
Site settings, generated pages and the `llms.txt` files now take their build directory from the project's layout. This changes nothing for site authors; builds are unchanged.

Each of these writers took a directory argument, and every caller passed it the layout's build directory. The directory was a second source of truth for a location the layout already owns, so a caller could pass one that disagreed with it.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: remove the exclude_* functions in favour of %nodoc
description:
The renderer no longer offers `exclude_parameters`, `exclude_attributes`, `exclude_functions`, `exclude_classes` and `exclude_type_aliases`, nor the module state behind them. To leave a member out of the API reference, write `%nodoc` in its docstring.

The directive already does the job of the four member functions, so the renderer had two mechanisms for one purpose, and the module state was one of two that renderers read. Nothing in the gauntlet packages, the docs, any configuration, the skills or the tests called any of the five. A site that never called them renders unchanged.

`exclude_parameters` has no replacement, because a parameter has no docstring to carry the directive. A `%nodoc_param` directive is filed as a follow-up.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: check examples when Quarto output is not valid UTF-8
description:
`great-docs check-examples` now checks a page whose Quarto output contains invalid UTF-8, instead of reporting it as an error.

It decoded Quarto's output with the locale encoding, so undecodable bytes raised `UnicodeDecodeError`, and the page's cells were never checked. Output is now read as UTF-8 with undecodable bytes replaced, as in other Quarto runs. This stacks on the timeout help change, which edits the same `quarto render` call.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: build API snapshots from the exports griffe expands
description:
Top-level API snapshots now take their names from the package's `__all__` after griffe expands it, and no longer fail on exports they cannot resolve.

Three cases went wrong. A package with `from .sub import __all__` got an empty snapshot, because the names came from the import's tokens. `__all__ = _names` crashed the snapshot with `TypeError: unhashable type`. A documented export pointing at a missing module raised `AliasResolutionError`, although the same case is already documented as `None` elsewhere. The snapshot feeds `great-docs api-diff`, the MCP API-diff tool and version badges.

This stacks on the tagged snapshot search change, which edits the same imports.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: find packages in src, python and lib in tagged API snapshots
description:
API snapshots at a git tag now search the project root and its `src`, `python` and `lib` directories as they were at the tag, the same order working-tree snapshots use. They also accept a dotted module name such as `firebird.base`.

Before, a tagged snapshot looked only at `<name>/` and `src/<name>/`, so a package under `python` or `lib`, or named by a dotted module, produced no snapshot and the comparison said it could not build one. This affected `great-docs api-diff`, `great-docs api-snapshot`, the MCP API-diff tool and version badges in versioned builds. Git paths were also taken from the repository root, so a project in a repository subdirectory never got tagged snapshots.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: report invalid MCP tool arguments as failed tool results
description:
The MCP server now validates every tool call against the tool's input schema before running it. A call with a wrongly typed argument, such as `gd_lint` with `checks: 5`, now returns a failed tool result listing each problem, so the model can correct the call.

Before, only missing required arguments were checked. A wrongly typed one raised inside the tool and reached the client as a protocol error. Arguments a schema does not declare are still accepted.

The `mcp` extra now declares `jsonschema>=4.20.0`, which Great Docs imports directly and mcp already requires. This stacks on the adapter typing change, which touches the same call path.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: docs: describe check-examples --timeout as a page render limit
description:
The help text for `great-docs check-examples --timeout` now says what the option does. It called the value a per-cell timeout, but Quarto's Jupyter engine applies no limit to a single cell. The option bounds each page's render at the timeout times the page's cell count, plus 60 seconds. Its name, type, default and behaviour are unchanged.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: serialise generated page front matter as YAML
description:
The MCP page-creation tool, the tags index and the changelog now write their front matter as YAML, which quotes a value only when it needs quoting.

They interpolated the title inside double quotes without escaping. A title containing a quote, which an MCP caller can supply, wrote a page with invalid front matter. Translated strings hold no quotes today, so only that tool could break, but the other two would on the next translation that did.

Pages render the same, but a title that needed no quotes is no longer quoted: `title: "Site Tags"` becomes `title: Site Tags` in the generated `tags/index.qmd`. The Quarto project diff shows that one line, so this PR goes without the fail-on-difference marker. It stacks on the layout change, which edits the changelog writer.

title: build: declare packaging as a direct dependency
description:
`packaging>=22` is now a direct dependency of Great Docs.

Great Docs imports `packaging` to parse requirements in project metadata and to compare an installed agent skill's version with its own. It was installed only because `ipykernel` requires it, so a change in `ipykernel`'s requirements could break those features. The lower bound matches `ipykernel`'s.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: reload edited source during watch rebuilds
description:
Watch rebuilds now pick up an edit that Python's bytecode cache would hide.

A rebuild drops the package's modules and imports them again, but Python validates a cached `.pyc` by the source's modification time, in whole seconds, and its size. An edit saved in the same second as the previous compile, with the file size unchanged, loaded the old bytecode, and the preview kept the old docstring until the next edit. Rebuilds now discard the cached bytecode of the modules they forget.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: proofread the pages inside a directory argument
description:
`great-docs proofread recipes/` now checks the `.qmd` and `.md` pages under the directory, recursively. Paths with a part below the directory that starts with `_` or `.` are skipped, the rule the build uses for page directories.

Before, a directory argument was skipped, nothing was checked, and the JSON still reported a checked file. The user guide had been changed to recommend a glob for this reason. `--docs-dir` was documented as relative to the project root but resolved against the working directory, so with `--project-path` pointing elsewhere it read the wrong place, and its search also read copies under `_site`, `_freeze` and `.quarto`. It now resolves against the project root and uses the same skip rule.

`files_checked` in the JSON now counts only the files given to Harper. The user guide and recipe describe the directory search and the default inputs.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: refactor: drop an unreachable fallback from Go command summaries
description:
Go command summaries no longer carry a branch that cannot run. Generated summaries are unchanged.

The helper uses the first sentence when it fits the length limit. The removed branch returned the whole description when it fitted, but it was reached only after the first sentence, a prefix of the description, had exceeded the limit. The Rust copy of the helper lost this branch earlier.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: omit the type label on plain text CLI arguments
description:
CLI reference pages no longer show a type on plain text arguments. Options keep theirs, `TEXT` included.

The extractor's docstring said an argument's type is left out for text, but the check compared Click's lower-case type name with `"TEXT"`, so it never matched. Click text arguments showed `TEXT` and Typer `str` arguments showed `STR`. This changes the CLI pages of every Click and Typer package with a text argument, so the PR goes without the fail-on-difference marker. The CLI guide's list of page sections now mentions the omission.

title: fix: keep Python API snapshots when an old release's CLI fails to import
description:
A release whose CLI module raises `ValueError` or `TypeError` on import now gets no CLI snapshot, and its Python API snapshot is kept. Before, the error escaped.

This happens when an old release imports under newer dependencies. The `%evolution` marker, `great-docs api-diff`, the MCP API-diff tool and version badges then raised instead of covering the Python API. The Quarto shortcode already rendered the table in this case, so the marker and the shortcode now agree.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: detect MCPServer when discovering MCP servers
description:
Automatic MCP server discovery now finds servers built with `MCPServer`, the class that replaced `FastMCP` in mcp 2. Before, such a server was skipped and got no reference pages unless the configuration named its variable, though the README and user guide promised detection.

The user guide also said introspection calls "the server's internal handlers". It runs the server over stdio and queries it through the protocol, with a source scan for tools as the fallback. The README, guide and home page tile now name the types detected and describe that.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: fix: keep a separate freeze cache for each documentation version
description:
Versioned builds now keep one `_freeze/` cache per version, so each version reuses the results it computed on the previous build.

Every version rendered with its own cache, but the build merged them all into one `_freeze/` directory keyed by page path. Where several versions contained the same page, only one entry survived, and the other versions re-executed that page on every build. With six versions sharing a page, five missed the cache each time. Output was never wrong, because Quarto checks a hit against the page's content hash, but builds were slower than they needed to be.

The latest version, and any build without versions, still caches at the top of `_freeze/`. Older versions cache under `_freeze/_versions/<build directory>/`. Single-version projects see no change. The rendered pages do not change either, but the Quarto project diff shows the new restore script in each project, so this PR goes without the fail-on-difference marker.

title: fix: skip user guide pages named outside the guide directory
description:
An explicit `user_guide:` list now warns about an entry that is absolute or contains a `..` component, and skips it as it does a missing file.

Before, an absolute entry made the sidebar step raise a `ValueError` and stopped the build, and a `..` entry published its page outside `user-guide/`.

<!-- quarto-project-diff: fail-on difference -->

title: Add the site tools to the WebMCP runtime
description:
This PR adds four read-only WebMCP tools to `webmcp.js`: `get_site_overview`, `list_pages`, `get_page` and `search_docs`. They read the site's `gd-webmcp.json` on first use and fetch `search.json` only when a search or section lookup needs it, and every result carries an absolute URL.

`get_page` resolves a page by path or URL, API name or alias, title, file name and then shared words, returning `ambiguous` with candidates when matches are close. It can return a single section, found by anchor (including the rendered page's anchors, mapped through `search.json`) or by heading text, and long pages are truncated with their outline.

`search_docs` ranks page sections by phrase and word matches in titles, headings and text, boosts the page of an exact API name, caps results at two per page, and accepts a scope of a kind of page or a section. Failures come back as data: `fetch_failed` lists fallback files, and `not_found` includes candidates or a hint.
